Use it during the development and integration phase to monitor task starvation or stack overflows. Warning: Enabling this in production code can significantly degrade real-time performance and increase interrupt latency due to the high volume of serial data transmission.

DUMP_TASK_HDR.brief: Enables or disables the inclusion of task control block headers in system memory dumps.
DUMP_TASK_HDR.notes: When set to 0x01, the scheduler appends task metadata (such as stack pointers and state) to crash dumps. Disabling this (0x00) reduces the size of the dump file but makes debugging task-related crashes significantly harder. It depends on the system's logging or debug interface being initialized.
DUMP_TASK_HDR.usage: Enable this flag during the development and testing phases to facilitate post-mortem debugging of task stack overflows or deadlocks. Disable it in production builds if memory constraints are extremely tight or if you need to minimize the footprint of diagnostic data.

DUMP_TASK_REG.brief: Enables the inclusion of CPU register snapshots in task dump reports during system crashes.
DUMP_TASK_REG.notes: When enabled (non-zero), the scheduler saves the current CPU register state to the task control block upon a fault. This flag requires sufficient stack space to store the register context. It is typically used in conjunction with a debugger or a serial logging utility to perform post-mortem analysis.
DUMP_TASK_REG.usage: Enable this flag during the development and debugging phase to identify the exact instruction pointer and register values at the moment of a task crash. Disable it in production builds to save RAM and reduce the overhead of context switching and exception handling.

DUMP_TASK_STACK.brief: Enables the automatic dumping of task stack memory contents to the debug console upon a task crash or stack overflow event.
DUMP_TASK_STACK.notes: When enabled (0x08), the kernel triggers a memory dump of the task's stack area to the UART/ITM interface during a fault. This flag depends on the system having a configured debug output stream. Typical values are 0x00 (disabled) or 0x08 (enabled). Enabling this increases the size of the fault handler code and may slightly increase the time spent in the error recovery routine.
DUMP_TASK_STACK.usage: Enable this flag during the development and debugging phase to identify the root cause of stack overflows or memory corruption. Disable it in production builds to reduce binary size and prevent sensitive data from being printed to the debug interface.

DUMP_TASK_STATS.brief: Enables the collection and reporting of CPU usage and stack depth statistics for individual tasks.
DUMP_TASK_STATS.notes: When enabled (0x10), the scheduler tracks execution time and stack high-water marks for each task. This increases memory overhead per task control block (TCB) and adds a small CPU cycle penalty to context switches. It requires the system heap to be initialized and is typically used in conjunction with a debug console or telemetry module.
DUMP_TASK_STATS.usage: Enable this flag during the development and profiling phase to identify tasks that are starving the CPU or nearing stack overflow. Disable it in production builds to save RAM and improve real-time performance. Ensure that your task stack sizes are large enough to accommodate the extra overhead if this flag is enabled.

ECDSA_P256_HASH_SIZE.brief: Defines the fixed byte length of the hash used in ECDSA P-256 signature operations.
ECDSA_P256_HASH_SIZE.notes: This constant is set to 32 bytes, which corresponds to the 256-bit output size of the SHA-256 algorithm. It is a hard requirement for the ca_ecdsa_p256_sign_hash and ca_ecdsa_p256_verify_hash functions. Changing this value will cause cryptographic mismatches and likely lead to runtime errors or failed signature verifications.
ECDSA_P256_HASH_SIZE.usage: Do not modify this value. It is fixed by the ECDSA P-256 standard (FIPS 186-4). If you are implementing a custom signing flow, ensure your input buffer matches this size exactly before calling ca_ecdsa_p256_sign_hash.

ECDSA_P256_LIMBS.brief: Defines the number of 64-bit limbs used to represent the P-256 elliptic curve coordinates.
ECDSA_P256_LIMBS.notes: This constant determines the memory footprint and computational complexity of ECDSA P-256 operations. A value of 8U corresponds to 512 bits (8 * 64 bits), which is the standard representation for the 256-bit prime field used in NIST P-256. Changing this value will break the cryptographic implementation and cause runtime errors in ca_ecdsa_p256_* functions.
ECDSA_P256_LIMBS.usage: Do not modify this value. It is a fixed architectural constant required by the underlying math library to correctly process P-256 keys and signatures. If you encounter memory constraints, look at other system parameters rather than altering cryptographic limb counts.

ECDSA_P256_PRIVATE_SIZE.brief: Defines the fixed byte length of a P-256 elliptic curve private key.
ECDSA_P256_PRIVATE_SIZE.notes: This constant is set to 32 bytes, which corresponds to 256 bits. It is a fundamental requirement for the ca_ecdsa_p256_* family of functions. Changing this value will cause buffer overflows or cryptographic failures in any function expecting a standard NIST P-256 key, as the underlying math relies on this specific size.
ECDSA_P256_PRIVATE_SIZE.usage: This value should not be changed. It is used to allocate memory buffers for private keys when calling ca_ecdsa_p256_keygen or when passing private keys to signing functions. If you are handling raw key data, use this constant to ensure your buffers are correctly sized: uint8_t my_key[ECDSA_P256_PRIVATE_SIZE];

ECDSA_P256_PUBLIC_SIZE.brief: Defines the fixed byte length of an ECDSA P-256 public key in the caOS crypto stack.
ECDSA_P256_PUBLIC_SIZE.notes: This constant is set to 64 bytes, representing the concatenation of the X and Y coordinates (32 bytes each) of the elliptic curve point. It is used by ca_ecdsa_p256_verify and related functions to validate buffer sizes. Changing this value will cause buffer overflows or validation failures in the cryptographic subsystem, as the underlying hardware/software implementation expects exactly 64 bytes for uncompressed P-256 public keys.
ECDSA_P256_PUBLIC_SIZE.usage: Do not change this value. It is a protocol-defined constant for the NIST P-256 curve. If you are handling public keys, ensure your buffers are allocated with this size using ca_memory_allocate(ECDSA_P256_PUBLIC_SIZE) to prevent memory corruption.

ECDSA_P256_SIGNATURE_SIZE.brief: Defines the fixed byte length of an ECDSA P-256 digital signature.
ECDSA_P256_SIGNATURE_SIZE.notes: The value 64 represents the concatenation of two 32-byte integers (r and s) that constitute a standard ECDSA signature on the P-256 curve. This constant is used for buffer allocation and validation checks in cryptographic operations. It is a fixed protocol requirement and should not be modified.
ECDSA_P256_SIGNATURE_SIZE.usage: Use this constant when allocating buffers for signature storage or when passing length arguments to functions like ca_ecdsa_p256_sign or ca_ecdsa_p256_verify. Do not change this value, as it is mathematically tied to the P-256 curve specification; changing it will cause cryptographic failures.

ED25519_PUBLIC_SIZE.brief: Defines the fixed byte length of an Ed25519 public key in the caOS cryptographic library.
ED25519_PUBLIC_SIZE.notes: This constant is set to 32 bytes, which is the standard size for Ed25519 public keys as per RFC 8032. Changing this value will cause buffer overflows or cryptographic verification failures in any function expecting a standard Ed25519 key. It is a hard-coded dependency for all signing and verification routines within the caOS crypto stack.
ED25519_PUBLIC_SIZE.usage: Do not modify this value unless you are implementing a non-standard variant of the Ed25519 algorithm. It is used to allocate memory for key storage and to define the bounds for array copies. If you encounter 'invalid key size' errors, ensure your input buffer matches this constant exactly.

ED25519_SEED_SIZE.brief: Defines the fixed byte length of the seed used for generating Ed25519 cryptographic keys.
ED25519_SEED_SIZE.notes: This constant is set to 32 bytes (256 bits), which is the standard requirement for the Ed25519 algorithm. Changing this value will cause cryptographic functions to fail or produce invalid keys, as the underlying library expects exactly 32 bytes of entropy. It has no dependencies on other RTOS flags but is critical for all secure communication modules.
ED25519_SEED_SIZE.usage: Do not change this value under normal circumstances. It should only be modified if you are implementing a custom cryptographic wrapper that requires a different input size, though this is highly discouraged as it breaks compatibility with standard Ed25519 implementations. Ensure any buffer allocated for the seed is exactly this size to prevent memory overflows.

ED25519_SIGNATURE_SIZE.brief: Defines the fixed byte length of an Ed25519 digital signature.
ED25519_SIGNATURE_SIZE.notes: This constant is set to 64 bytes, which is the standard size for Ed25519 signatures as per RFC 8032. Changing this value will cause cryptographic verification functions to fail or trigger buffer overflows if the underlying memory buffers are not resized accordingly. It is a hard-coded requirement for the Ed25519 algorithm implementation in caOS.
ED25519_SIGNATURE_SIZE.usage: Do not modify this value unless you are porting a non-standard variant of the Ed25519 algorithm. It is used to allocate stack or heap memory for signature storage. Ensure that any buffers passed to signing or verification functions are at least this size to prevent memory corruption.

ENABLE_CLI.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) module for real-time system debugging and interaction via UART.
ENABLE_CLI.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the CLI task and allocates memory for command buffers. Disabling it (0) reduces flash memory usage and frees up CPU cycles. This flag depends on the UART driver being initialized in the hardware abstraction layer.
ENABLE_CLI.usage: Enable this during development to inspect task states, memory usage, and system variables in real-time. Disable it in production builds to save memory and prevent unauthorized access to system commands.

ENABLE_CLI_STDOUT.brief: Enables or disables the redirection of the Command Line Interface (CLI) output to the standard output (STDOUT) stream.
ENABLE_CLI_STDOUT.notes: When set to 1, all CLI responses are routed to the system's default serial output (usually UART). If set to 0, the CLI will not print any feedback to the console. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) being initialized for UART communication. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
ENABLE_CLI_STDOUT.usage: Enable this during development to debug system commands and view task status via a serial terminal. Disable it in production builds to reduce CPU overhead and prevent sensitive system information from being exposed through the serial port.

ENABLE_DBG_UART.brief: Enables the dedicated debug UART peripheral for system logging and RTOS kernel diagnostics.
ENABLE_DBG_UART.notes: When enabled, the RTOS redirects kernel trace messages and system assertions to the hardware UART port. Disabling this flag saves CPU cycles and reduces power consumption by stopping the UART peripheral and associated DMA/interrupt overhead. It requires the corresponding UART pins to be physically connected to a serial-to-USB adapter on your development board.
ENABLE_DBG_UART.usage: Enable this during the development and debugging phase to monitor system health and catch runtime errors via a serial terminal. Disable this flag in production builds to minimize binary size and prevent potential security leaks of internal system states through the debug port.

ENABLE_ITM.brief: Enables or disables the Instrumentation Trace Macrocell (ITM) for real-time debugging output.
ENABLE_ITM.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS redirects system logs and trace data to the ITM port, allowing high-speed debugging via an SWO pin. When set to 0, this feature is disabled, saving CPU cycles and memory. This flag requires the hardware debugger to support SWO tracing and the corresponding pin to be configured in the MCU.
ENABLE_ITM.usage: Enable this (set to 1) when you need to monitor task switching or system events in real-time without stopping the CPU. Disable it (set to 0) for production builds to reduce code size and prevent potential timing issues caused by trace overhead. Ensure your debugger is connected to the SWO pin before enabling.

ENABLE_SENSOR.brief: Global master switch to enable or disable the sensor driver subsystem within the caOS kernel.
ENABLE_SENSOR.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes sensor-related tasks and hardware abstraction layers. When set to 0, all sensor-related code is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage. This flag is a prerequisite for other sensor-specific configurations like SENSOR_POLLING_RATE and SENSOR_I2C_ADDRESS.
ENABLE_SENSOR.usage: Set to 1 during standard development to enable sensor data acquisition. Set to 0 if your specific hardware variant does not include sensors or if you need to free up memory space. Ensure this is enabled before attempting to call any sensor API functions, otherwise, the linker will report undefined references.

ENABLE_STDOUT.brief: Enables or disables the redirection of standard output (printf) to the UART peripheral.
ENABLE_STDOUT.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the hardware UART and routes stdout to it. When set to 0, all printf calls are ignored or redirected to a null device. This flag depends on the UART_PORT_CONFIG being defined in the hardware abstraction layer. Typical values are 0 (production) or 1 (debugging).
ENABLE_STDOUT.usage: Enable this during development to view system logs and debug messages via a serial terminal. Disable it before deploying to production to save CPU cycles, reduce power consumption, and prevent potential blocking issues if the UART buffer becomes full.

ENABLE_UART.brief: Enables or disables the hardware abstraction layer for UART communication within the RTOS.
ENABLE_UART.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes UART peripherals and includes driver code in the build. When set to 0, all UART-related functions are excluded, reducing the binary footprint. This flag must be enabled if your application uses serial debugging, logging, or external UART-based sensors.
ENABLE_UART.usage: Set to 1 if your project requires serial communication or console logging. Set to 0 to save flash memory and RAM if UART is not used. Warning: disabling this will cause compilation errors if your application code calls any UART-related API functions.

EN_ADC.brief: Enables the Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) driver subsystem within the caOS RTOS.
EN_ADC.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes ADC hardware abstraction layers and allocates necessary memory for ADC peripheral management. If set to 0, all ADC-related API calls will return an error code or trigger a hard fault. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) being correctly configured in the STM32CubeMX project settings.
EN_ADC.usage: Set this to 1 when your application requires reading analog sensors or voltage levels. Disable it (set to 0) to save flash memory and RAM if your project does not use any ADC channels. Ensure that the corresponding ADC clock is enabled in the system clock configuration before enabling this flag.

EN_AES.brief: Enables hardware-accelerated AES encryption support within the caOS kernel and middleware.
EN_AES.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the STM32 hardware cryptographic peripheral and links the AES driver to the OS task scheduler. Disabling this (0) reduces the binary footprint and saves RAM by excluding the crypto-library stack. This flag depends on the target MCU having a hardware AES engine; if enabled on a device without one, the system will trigger a hard fault during initialization.
EN_AES.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires secure data transmission (e.g., TLS, encrypted storage, or secure boot). Change this to 0 if your project does not use encryption to optimize memory usage. Warning: Ensure the STM32 model supports hardware AES before setting this to 1, otherwise the kernel will fail to boot.

EN_AES_CHANNEL_SERVICE.brief: Enables the hardware-accelerated AES encryption service within the caOS kernel.
EN_AES_CHANNEL_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the STM32 hardware cryptographic peripheral and exposes the AES API for task-level encryption. Disabling this (0) reduces the kernel memory footprint and removes the dependency on the hardware crypto driver. This flag requires the STM32 hardware to have a built-in AES peripheral. The AES channel service also enables secure key management and hardware-accelerated cryptographic operations that significantly improve performance compared to software implementations.
EN_AES_CHANNEL_SERVICE.usage: Enable this when your application requires secure data transmission or storage (e.g., TLS, encrypted logging, secure boot). Change this to 0 if you are running on a low-power device without crypto hardware or if you need to save flash memory space. Ensure that the corresponding hardware clock is enabled in the system initialization if this flag is set to 1. Warning: Setting this to 1 on devices without AES hardware will cause kernel initialization failure. Typical use cases include IoT devices requiring secure communication, embedded systems with security requirements, and applications handling sensitive data where performance is critical.

EN_AES_GCM_SW_TEST.brief: Enables the software-based implementation of the AES-GCM cryptographic algorithm for testing purposes.
EN_AES_GCM_SW_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the software library for AES-GCM encryption and decryption. If set to 0, the software implementation is excluded to save flash memory. This flag is independent of hardware-accelerated AES modules but may conflict if hardware drivers are improperly initialized. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_AES_GCM_SW_TEST.usage: Enable this flag during the development and validation phase to verify cryptographic logic without relying on specific STM32 hardware peripherals. Disable it in production builds to reduce binary size and memory footprint, especially if hardware acceleration is available or if AES-GCM is not required by the application.

EN_ARP_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) service within the caOS network stack.
EN_ARP_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS handles ARP requests and responses to map IP addresses to MAC addresses. Disabling this (0) will prevent the device from communicating over Ethernet unless static ARP entries are manually managed. This flag depends on the underlying Ethernet driver being initialized and the TCP/IP stack being active.
EN_ARP_SERVICE.usage: Enable this (1) for standard network communication where the device needs to discover or respond to other nodes on the local network. Disable it (0) only in highly specialized, static-network environments where you want to minimize memory footprint or prevent the device from responding to network discovery traffic.

EN_BARRIER.brief: Enables or disables the synchronization barrier primitive within the caOS RTOS kernel.
EN_BARRIER.notes: When set to 1, the kernel includes code for barrier objects, allowing multiple tasks to wait until a specified number of threads have reached a synchronization point. Disabling this (0) reduces the total flash memory footprint by removing the barrier management logic. This flag has no direct dependencies on other kernel objects but is required if your application uses barrier-based task coordination.
EN_BARRIER.usage: Enable this flag if your application architecture requires multiple tasks to synchronize at a specific execution gate before proceeding. You should disable it if your project is memory-constrained and does not utilize barriers to save code space. Ensure that all tasks intended to use barriers are initialized correctly after enabling this flag to avoid null pointer dereferences.

EN_BIG_E.brief: Configures the system to use Big-Endian byte order for data storage and memory access.
EN_BIG_E.notes: When enabled (1), the system stores the most significant byte at the lowest memory address. When disabled (0), it defaults to Little-Endian. This flag must match the hardware architecture and the endianness of any external communication protocols (like network packets or specific sensors) to prevent data corruption.
EN_BIG_E.usage: Change this value only if your specific STM32 hardware configuration or external peripheral communication requires Big-Endian format. Incorrectly setting this flag will cause multi-byte variables (like uint32_t) to be read or written in reverse, leading to critical logic errors and system instability.

EN_BLAKE2S.brief: Enables or disables the BLAKE2s cryptographic hash function support in the caOS kernel.
EN_BLAKE2S.notes: When set to 1, the ca_blake2s_* API functions are compiled into the binary. When set to 0, these functions are excluded, reducing the total flash memory footprint. This flag is a prerequisite for using HMAC-BLAKE2s functions.
EN_BLAKE2S.usage: Enable this flag only if your application requires BLAKE2s hashing for data integrity or security protocols. If your project does not use BLAKE2s, keep it at 0 to save flash space. Example usage: ca_blake2s_init(&ctx); ca_blake2s_update(&ctx, data, len); ca_blake2s_final(&ctx, hash);

EN_BLAKE2S_TEST.brief: Enables or disables the self-test routine for the BLAKE2s cryptographic hash algorithm.
EN_BLAKE2S_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the system executes the ca_blake2s_selftest function during the boot sequence or initialization phase. This flag has no direct dependencies on other modules but increases the startup time and code size slightly. The valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_BLAKE2S_TEST.usage: Change this value to 1 during development or production validation to ensure the BLAKE2s implementation is functioning correctly on the target hardware. It is recommended to set this to 0 in final production firmware to save flash memory and reduce boot time, unless periodic integrity verification is required by your security policy.

EN_BLOCK_POOL.brief: Enables the memory block pool allocator for fixed-size memory management.
EN_BLOCK_POOL.notes: When set to 1, the kernel includes the block pool API, allowing for deterministic, fragmentation-free memory allocation. Disabling it (0) removes this functionality to save flash and RAM. It requires the system heap to be initialized if dynamic pool creation is used.
EN_BLOCK_POOL.usage: Enable this when your application requires high-speed, predictable memory allocation for tasks or message buffers. Use this instead of standard malloc() to prevent heap fragmentation. Ensure sufficient RAM is allocated for the pool size defined in your task configuration.

EN_BOOT_IMAGE.brief: Enables or disables the bootloader image verification and update management features.
EN_BOOT_IMAGE.notes: When set to 1, the system includes support for bootloader image slots and update verification via the ca_boot_* API. When set to 0, these features are excluded from the build, reducing the binary size. This flag is typically used in conjunction with flash memory partitioning. If enabled, ensure the memory map is correctly defined to accommodate multiple image slots.
EN_BOOT_IMAGE.usage: Set this to 1 only if your application requires remote firmware updates or a secure bootloader mechanism. If you are developing a simple application that does not require field updates, keep this at 0 to save flash space and simplify the boot process. Warning: Enabling this without proper flash layout configuration will cause the system to fail during the boot sequence.

EN_CAN.brief: Enables or disables the Controller Area Network (CAN) peripheral driver support within the RTOS.
EN_CAN.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes CAN hardware abstraction layers and allocates memory for CAN message queues. When set to 0, the CAN driver is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage. This flag must be enabled if your application uses CAN communication; otherwise, calling CAN-related API functions will result in linker errors or undefined behavior.
EN_CAN.usage: Set this to 1 only if your hardware design includes a CAN transceiver and your application requires CAN bus communication. Keep it at 0 for projects that do not use CAN to save system resources and minimize the binary footprint. Ensure that the corresponding hardware clock configuration is enabled in the system initialization if this flag is set to 1.

EN_CHACHA20_POLY1305.brief: Enables or disables the ChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption algorithm support in the caOS kernel.
EN_CHACHA20_POLY1305.notes: When set to 1, the caOS library includes the implementation of ChaCha20-Poly1305 (e.g., ca_chacha20poly1305_encrypt). Enabling this increases the firmware binary size due to the inclusion of cryptographic primitives. It is typically disabled (0) by default to save flash memory on resource-constrained STM32 devices if the application does not require secure authenticated communication.
EN_CHACHA20_POLY1305.usage: Change this value to 1 only if your application needs to perform authenticated encryption or decryption using the ChaCha20-Poly1305 suite. If you attempt to call ca_chacha20poly1305_* functions while this flag is 0, the linker will report an undefined reference error.

EN_CHACHA20_POLY1305_TEST.brief: Enables or disables the self-test routines for the ChaCha20-Poly1305 cryptographic algorithm.
EN_CHACHA20_POLY1305_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the system executes a verification test for ChaCha20-Poly1305 during the boot or initialization phase. If set to 0, the test is skipped, reducing boot time and code size. This flag is independent of the actual implementation of the algorithm but is required to ensure the integrity of the crypto library before use.
EN_CHACHA20_POLY1305_TEST.usage: Change this value to 1 during the development and debugging phase to verify that the ChaCha20-Poly1305 implementation is functioning correctly on the target hardware. Set it to 0 in production builds to optimize startup performance and save flash memory, provided that the algorithm has been validated during the testing phase.

EN_CLI_ADC.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) integration for real-time ADC peripheral monitoring and debugging.
EN_CLI_ADC.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the ADC command parser, allowing users to read raw values or status via the serial console. This requires the UART driver to be active and consumes additional stack space in the CLI task. If set to 0, the ADC CLI commands are excluded from the binary, reducing flash memory usage.
EN_CLI_ADC.usage: Enable this during the development and testing phase to verify sensor data or troubleshoot ADC hardware issues without needing an external debugger. Disable it in production builds to save memory and prevent unauthorized access to hardware registers via the console.

EN_CLI_ARP.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) support for Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) commands.
EN_CLI_ARP.notes: When set to 1, the system includes code to inspect and manipulate the ARP table via the serial console. Disabling this (0) reduces the firmware binary size and memory footprint. It depends on the network stack being initialized and the CLI module being active.
EN_CLI_ARP.usage: Enable this during the development and debugging phase to verify network connectivity and troubleshoot IP-to-MAC address mapping issues. Disable it in production builds to save flash memory and prevent unauthorized network table manipulation.

EN_CLI_BLAKE2S.brief: Enables or disables the BLAKE2s hashing command within the Command Line Interface (CLI).
EN_CLI_BLAKE2S.notes: When set to 1, the CLI will include commands to compute BLAKE2s hashes directly from the console. This increases the firmware binary size due to the inclusion of the BLAKE2s algorithm implementation. It depends on the ca_cli_* and ca_blake2s_* API modules being available in the build.
EN_CLI_BLAKE2S.usage: Set to 1 if you need to perform runtime integrity checks or generate hashes via the serial console for debugging or security verification. Keep at 0 for production builds where CLI space is limited or if hashing functionality is not required by the end-user.

EN_CLI_CALLTO.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) call-to-function feature for interactive system debugging.
EN_CLI_CALLTO.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS includes the command parser module, allowing users to trigger specific system functions via a serial terminal. This increases the binary size (Flash usage) and requires a configured UART peripheral. If set to 0, the CLI code is excluded from the build, saving memory but disabling interactive runtime control.
EN_CLI_CALLTO.usage: Enable this during the development and integration phase to inspect task states, memory usage, or trigger manual tests without recompiling. Disable it in production builds to save Flash space and prevent unauthorized access to system functions via the serial port.

EN_CLI_CAN.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) functionality over the CAN bus.
EN_CLI_CAN.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the CAN peripheral to listen for and respond to diagnostic or control commands. This requires the CAN driver to be configured in the hardware abstraction layer. If set to 0, the CAN-based CLI task is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage and freeing up CAN message buffers.
EN_CLI_CAN.usage: Set to 1 during development or field maintenance to allow remote debugging and parameter tuning via CAN. Set to 0 in production firmware if the CAN bus is reserved exclusively for application-specific communication or to prevent unauthorized access to system commands.

EN_CLI_CAPTURE.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) input capture feature for real-time system debugging.
EN_CLI_CAPTURE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS allocates a dedicated buffer and interrupt handler to capture serial input commands. Disabling it (0) saves RAM and reduces CPU overhead. This feature depends on the UART driver being initialized and requires sufficient heap space for the command buffer.
EN_CLI_CAPTURE.usage: Enable this during the development and integration phase to allow runtime inspection of system variables and task states via a terminal. Disable it in production builds to minimize memory footprint and prevent unauthorized access to system commands.

EN_CLI_CHACHA20_POLY1305.brief: Enables or disables the ChaCha20-Poly1305 cryptographic commands in the CLI.
EN_CLI_CHACHA20_POLY1305.notes: When set to 1, the CLI will include commands to perform ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption and decryption. When set to 0 (default), these commands are excluded from the build to save flash memory. This flag does not affect the underlying library functions (ca_chacha20poly1305_*), only their exposure via the CLI interface.
EN_CLI_CHACHA20_POLY1305.usage: Enable this flag only if you need to perform manual cryptographic testing or debugging via the serial console. If your application does not require runtime access to these specific crypto operations, keep it at 0 to minimize the firmware footprint.

EN_CLI_CONFIG.brief: Enables or disables the Command Line Interface (CLI) module within the caOS RTOS.
EN_CLI_CONFIG.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the CLI task and serial communication buffers, allowing runtime debugging and command execution. Disabling it (0) reduces flash memory usage and RAM overhead by removing the command parser and associated buffers. This flag depends on the UART driver being correctly initialized in the hardware abstraction layer.
EN_CLI_CONFIG.usage: Set to 1 during development to interact with the system via a terminal for real-time monitoring and debugging. Set to 0 for production builds to save system resources and prevent unauthorized access to system commands. Ensure that the UART baud rate is configured correctly in the hardware settings before enabling this feature.

EN_CLI_CRC.brief: Enables or disables CRC verification for Command Line Interface (CLI) data packets.
EN_CLI_CRC.notes: When set to 1, the system calculates and validates a checksum for incoming CLI commands to ensure data integrity. If set to 0, the CRC check is bypassed, reducing CPU overhead but increasing the risk of executing corrupted commands. This flag requires the hardware CRC peripheral to be initialized in the system clock configuration.
EN_CLI_CRC.usage: Enable this (1) in production environments or noisy electrical conditions to prevent command corruption. Disable it (0) only during initial development or if the communication link is guaranteed to be error-free, as it saves a small amount of processing time per command.

EN_CLI_DAC.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) support for the Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) peripheral.
EN_CLI_DAC.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the DAC driver and registers CLI commands to control analog output levels. This flag depends on EN_CLI being enabled and requires the hardware DAC peripheral to be configured in the STM32 CubeMX project. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_DAC.usage: Enable this flag when you need to perform real-time testing or calibration of analog signals via the serial terminal. Change this to 0 if you need to save flash memory or if the DAC pins are being used for other purposes to avoid resource conflicts.

EN_CLI_DHCP.brief: Enables or disables the Command Line Interface (CLI) support for dynamic IP address assignment via DHCP.
EN_CLI_DHCP.notes: When set to 1, the system attempts to acquire an IP address from a network server during startup. If set to 0, the system ignores DHCP and relies on static IP configurations. This flag requires the network stack (LwIP) to be initialized and enabled in the project configuration.
EN_CLI_DHCP.usage: Enable this (1) when the device needs to connect to a network with a dynamic router. Disable it (0) for industrial or static environments where a fixed IP is mandatory to prevent connection delays or address conflicts.

EN_CLI_DMA.brief: Enables Direct Memory Access (DMA) for the Command Line Interface (CLI) peripheral communication.
EN_CLI_DMA.notes: When set to 1, the CLI uses DMA to handle data transmission and reception, offloading the CPU from byte-by-byte processing. When set to 0, the system reverts to interrupt-driven or polling mode. This flag requires the underlying hardware UART/USART peripheral to have DMA channels configured and available in the STM32 CubeMX project.
EN_CLI_DMA.usage: Enable this when the CLI is experiencing high latency or causing CPU bottlenecks during heavy logging or data transfer. Change to 0 only if you encounter DMA configuration conflicts or if the specific hardware peripheral does not support DMA. Ensure that the DMA buffer sizes are correctly defined in the system memory map to avoid memory corruption.

EN_CLI_DNS.brief: Enables or disables the Command Line Interface (CLI) DNS resolution module within the caOS RTOS.
EN_CLI_DNS.notes: When set to 1, the system includes code to resolve hostnames to IP addresses via the CLI. Enabling this increases the firmware binary size and requires a configured network stack (e.g., LwIP). If set to 0, DNS commands will be unavailable, saving flash memory and reducing stack usage.
EN_CLI_DNS.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires the ability to ping or connect to remote servers using domain names (e.g., 'google.com') directly from the serial console. Disable it if you are working on a memory-constrained device or if your application only uses static IP addresses to save resources.

EN_CLI_ECDSA_P256.brief: Enables or disables ECDSA P-256 cryptographic support within the Command Line Interface (CLI).
EN_CLI_ECDSA_P256.notes: When set to 1, the system includes code for ECDSA P-256 signature verification or generation via CLI commands. Setting this to 0 (default) excludes this functionality, reducing the binary size (Flash usage). This flag depends on the availability of the ca_ecdsa_* API set. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_ECDSA_P256.usage: Change this to 1 only if your application requires performing ECDSA P-256 cryptographic operations directly from the CLI (e.g., for remote device authentication or signature verification during field maintenance). If your application does not use these specific security features, keep it at 0 to save memory.

EN_CLI_ED25519.brief: Enables the ED25519 cryptographic signature verification module within the caOS Command Line Interface.
EN_CLI_ED25519.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the ED25519 library to verify signed commands or firmware updates. Enabling this increases the binary size by approximately 4KB and requires additional stack space for cryptographic calculations. It depends on the hardware abstraction layer providing a secure random number generator (RNG).
EN_CLI_ED25519.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires secure, authenticated remote command execution or signed bootloader verification. Disable it if you are constrained by flash memory or if your project does not require cryptographic security features to save system resources.

EN_CLI_ETH.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) over Ethernet for remote system debugging and configuration.
EN_CLI_ETH.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the TCP/IP stack and binds a telnet-like server to the CLI task. This requires the network stack (LwIP) to be enabled and configured. Disabling this (0) saves significant RAM and Flash memory by excluding the network driver and CLI processing buffers.
EN_CLI_ETH.usage: Enable this during development to allow remote access to system logs and shell commands without a physical serial cable. Disable it in production builds to reduce the attack surface and free up system resources.

EN_CLI_FAT.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) integration with the FAT filesystem module.
EN_CLI_FAT.notes: When set to 1, the system includes commands to interact with SD cards or flash storage (e.g., ls, cat, rm). Enabling this requires the FATFS library to be initialized and linked in the project. If disabled, the CLI will not recognize file-system-related commands, reducing the binary size.
EN_CLI_FAT.usage: Enable this flag when you need to perform file operations via the serial console for debugging or data logging. Ensure that the hardware abstraction layer for your storage medium (e.g., SPI/SDIO) is correctly configured before enabling, otherwise, the CLI commands will return error codes.

EN_CLI_FLASH.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) functionality stored in the device's internal Flash memory.
EN_CLI_FLASH.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the CLI module and allocates memory for command parsing; when 0, the CLI is disabled, reducing the binary size and RAM usage. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) flash driver being correctly configured in the project.
EN_CLI_FLASH.usage: Enable this during the development and debugging phase to interact with the system via a serial terminal. Disable it in production builds to save memory and prevent unauthorized access to system commands.

EN_CLI_GPIO.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) commands for real-time GPIO pin manipulation and status monitoring.
EN_CLI_GPIO.notes: When enabled, the system allocates memory for CLI command handlers related to hardware pins. Disabling this flag removes these commands from the firmware image, reducing the binary size and freeing up memory. It depends on the core CLI module being enabled in the OS configuration.
EN_CLI_GPIO.usage: Enable this during the development and debugging phase to toggle pins or check logic levels directly via a serial terminal without recompiling code. Disable it in production builds to save flash memory and prevent unauthorized hardware manipulation via the console.

EN_CLI_HTTP.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) access over the HTTP protocol.
EN_CLI_HTTP.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes a web-based terminal interface; when 0, the HTTP server component is excluded from the build to save flash memory and RAM. This flag requires the network stack (EN_NET_STACK) to be enabled. Typical values are 0 or 1.
EN_CLI_HTTP.usage: Enable this when you need to debug or configure the system remotely via a web browser. Disable it in production builds to reduce the attack surface and free up system resources. Ensure your network stack is correctly configured before enabling this, otherwise, the system may fail to initialize the network interface.

EN_CLI_HTTPS.brief: Enables or disables the HTTPS support within the command line interface (CLI) service.
EN_CLI_HTTPS.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the necessary code to handle HTTPS requests via the CLI. This flag depends on the underlying TLS stack being initialized. Disabling this (0) reduces the firmware binary size and memory footprint by excluding secure HTTP parsing logic. Typical value is 1 for secure remote management or 0 for resource-constrained devices.
EN_CLI_HTTPS.usage: Change this value to 1 when you need to perform secure remote configuration or firmware updates over the CLI. Set to 0 if you are running out of flash memory or if the device does not require encrypted network communication. Warning: Disabling this will cause any code calling ca_https_service_start to fail or result in a compilation error if the linker removes the associated symbols.

EN_CLI_I2C.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) commands for debugging and interacting with I2C peripherals.
EN_CLI_I2C.notes: When set to 1, the system includes code to scan, read, and write to I2C devices via the serial console. This increases the binary size and requires the I2C driver stack to be initialized. If set to 0, these commands are excluded from the build to save flash memory.
EN_CLI_I2C.usage: Enable this during the development and hardware bring-up phase to verify I2C sensor connectivity without writing custom test code. Disable it in production builds to reduce memory footprint and improve security by preventing unauthorized hardware access via the CLI.

EN_CLI_IPERF.brief: Enables the built-in Command Line Interface (CLI) module for network performance testing using iPerf.
EN_CLI_IPERF.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the iPerf server/client command set in the CLI. This requires the TCP/IP stack (LwIP) to be initialized and active. Disabling it (0) reduces the firmware binary size and frees up memory by removing the network testing overhead.
EN_CLI_IPERF.usage: Enable this during the development and network debugging phase to measure throughput and latency. Disable it in production builds to save flash memory and prevent unauthorized network testing commands from being executed.

EN_CLI_KSTORE.brief: Enables the persistent key-value storage module within the caOS Command Line Interface.
EN_CLI_KSTORE.notes: When set to 1, the system allocates memory for the KSTORE subsystem and initializes the flash-backed storage driver. Disabling this (0) removes the KSTORE commands from the CLI and frees up flash/RAM resources. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) flash driver being correctly configured in the board support package.
EN_CLI_KSTORE.usage: Enable this when you need to save system configuration parameters (like network settings or calibration offsets) that must persist across power cycles. Disable it if your application is memory-constrained or does not require non-volatile storage to save space. Warning: Ensure the flash sector addresses defined in the linker script do not overlap with the application code area when this is enabled.

EN_CLI_KSVC.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) kernel service for real-time system debugging and monitoring.
EN_CLI_KSVC.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes a dedicated task to process serial input commands. This requires an active UART peripheral configured in the hardware abstraction layer. Disabling this (0) saves approximately 2KB of Flash and 512 bytes of RAM, but removes the ability to inspect task states or system metrics at runtime.
EN_CLI_KSVC.usage: Enable this during the development and integration phases to monitor system health and task execution. Disable it in production builds to reduce memory footprint and eliminate potential security vulnerabilities associated with an exposed command interface.

EN_CLI_LED.brief: Enables or disables the visual feedback LED associated with the Command Line Interface (CLI) activity.
EN_CLI_LED.notes: When set to 1, the system toggles a dedicated GPIO pin whenever a command is received or processed via the CLI. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) having a valid LED pin definition in the board support package. Valid values are 1 (enabled) or 0 (disabled).
EN_CLI_LED.usage: Enable this during the initial bring-up phase to verify that the serial communication and CLI task are responding to input. Disable it in production builds to reduce CPU overhead and prevent unnecessary GPIO toggling if the LED is not physically present on the custom PCB.

EN_CLI_LPTIM.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) functionality using the Low Power Timer (LPTIM) peripheral.
EN_CLI_LPTIM.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the LPTIM to handle CLI timing and input processing. Disabling this (0) removes CLI support, reducing flash usage and power consumption. This flag depends on the hardware LPTIM peripheral being available and configured in the system clock tree.
EN_CLI_LPTIM.usage: Enable this when you need to debug the system via a serial console while in low-power modes. Change this to 0 if you are running out of memory or if the application does not require a user interface. Ensure the LPTIM clock source is correctly defined in the system initialization, otherwise, the CLI will remain unresponsive.

EN_CLI_MDNS.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) support for mDNS service discovery.
EN_CLI_MDNS.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the mDNS responder module, allowing the device to be discovered on the network via hostname. This requires the network stack (LwIP) to be active and configured. Disabling this (0) reduces flash memory usage and removes the mDNS background task.
EN_CLI_MDNS.usage: Enable this when you need to access the device via a friendly hostname (e.g., 'device.local') instead of a static IP address. Ensure that the network interface is initialized before this flag is enabled, otherwise, the system may hang during the mDNS startup sequence.

EN_CLI_MODBUS.brief: Enables the built-in Command Line Interface (CLI) support for Modbus protocol debugging and configuration.
EN_CLI_MODBUS.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS compiles the Modbus command parser into the system image. This increases Flash memory usage and requires an active UART or console peripheral. It depends on EN_CLI being enabled. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_MODBUS.usage: Enable this flag during the development and integration phase to monitor Modbus registers and troubleshoot communication issues via the serial console. Disable it in production builds to save Flash memory and improve system security by preventing unauthorized register access.

EN_CLI_MQTT.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) integration for MQTT protocol debugging and control.
EN_CLI_MQTT.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the MQTT command parser, allowing users to send MQTT-related commands via the serial console. This requires the network stack and MQTT client modules to be enabled. Disabling this (0) saves approximately 2KB of Flash memory and reduces RAM usage by removing the command buffer.
EN_CLI_MQTT.usage: Enable this during the development and integration phase to monitor MQTT connection status, publish test messages, or subscribe to topics manually. Disable this in production firmware to reduce the attack surface and free up system resources.

EN_CLI_NET.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) over network protocols like Telnet or TCP.
EN_CLI_NET.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the network stack and binds a CLI listener to a specific port. Disabling this (0) saves significant RAM and Flash memory by excluding network buffers and command parsing logic. It requires the network stack (e.g., LwIP) to be enabled in the project configuration.
EN_CLI_NET.usage: Enable this during development to allow remote debugging and system monitoring via a network terminal. Disable it in production firmware to reduce the attack surface and free up system resources.

EN_CLI_NTP.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) support for Network Time Protocol (NTP) synchronization commands.
EN_CLI_NTP.notes: When set to 1, the system includes CLI handlers to manually trigger or query NTP time synchronization. This flag depends on the network stack being initialized and the NTP client module being enabled in the build. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_NTP.usage: Enable this during the development and debugging phase to verify time synchronization status or force a time update via the serial console. Disable it in production builds to save flash memory and reduce the attack surface of the device.

EN_CLI_PWR.brief: Enables or disables the Command Line Interface (CLI) power management features.
EN_CLI_PWR.notes: When set to 1, the system allows the CLI to enter low-power sleep modes during idle periods. When set to 0, the CLI remains fully active, preventing the MCU from entering deep sleep states. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) power management module being initialized.
EN_CLI_PWR.usage: Enable this (1) when developing battery-powered devices to extend runtime. Disable it (0) during initial debugging or if you experience issues with the CLI becoming unresponsive after the system enters sleep mode.

EN_CLI_QSPI.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) functionality over the QSPI peripheral.
EN_CLI_QSPI.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the QSPI driver to handle serial communication commands. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) being configured for QSPI and sufficient heap memory allocation for the CLI buffer. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_QSPI.usage: Enable this flag when you need to debug or interact with the system via a QSPI-connected terminal. Change this to 0 if you need to save flash memory or if the QSPI pins are required for external memory storage instead of communication. Ensure the baud rate and pin mapping are correctly defined in the board support package before enabling.

EN_CLI_RNG.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) random number generator utility functions.
EN_CLI_RNG.notes: When set to 1, the system includes additional CLI commands to generate and display random values. This requires the hardware random number generator (RNG) peripheral to be initialized in the system clock configuration. If set to 0, the associated CLI commands are excluded from the binary, reducing flash memory usage.
EN_CLI_RNG.usage: Enable this flag during the development and debugging phase if you need to test entropy-based features or generate random test data via the serial console. Disable it in production builds to save memory and prevent unauthorized access to system entropy sources.

EN_CLI_ROUTE.brief: Enables the command-line interface (CLI) routing engine for processing system commands.
EN_CLI_ROUTE.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the CLI parser and routes incoming serial data to registered command handlers. Disabling this (0) removes the CLI task from the scheduler, saving RAM and CPU cycles. It depends on the UART driver being initialized and requires sufficient stack space for the CLI task.
EN_CLI_ROUTE.usage: Enable this during development to interact with the system via a terminal for debugging, runtime monitoring, or manual task control. Disable it in production builds to reduce the memory footprint and prevent unauthorized access to system commands.

EN_CLI_RTC.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) integration for the Real-Time Clock (RTC) peripheral.
EN_CLI_RTC.notes: When set to 1, the system registers RTC-specific commands (e.g., date/time setting, alarm configuration) into the shell. This requires the RTC peripheral to be initialized in the hardware abstraction layer. If set to 0, the RTC commands are excluded from the binary, reducing flash memory usage.
EN_CLI_RTC.usage: Enable this flag when you need to debug or manually adjust system time via the serial console. Disable it in production builds if the CLI is not required or to save memory. Ensure that the underlying RTC driver is enabled in the system configuration before setting this to 1, otherwise, the CLI commands will return errors.

EN_CLI_SDIO.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) communication over the SDIO peripheral.
EN_CLI_SDIO.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the SDIO hardware driver to route CLI input/output commands. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) being configured for SDIO and requires sufficient heap memory for the SDIO buffer. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_SDIO.usage: Enable this flag when you need to debug or interact with the system via an SD card interface or high-speed SDIO-based terminal. Change this to 0 if you are not using SDIO to save flash memory and RAM. Warning: Ensure the SDIO pins are not being used by other peripherals before enabling, as this will cause hardware conflicts.

EN_CLI_SHA256.brief: Enables or disables the SHA-256 cryptographic hashing module within the caOS Command Line Interface.
EN_CLI_SHA256.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the SHA-256 algorithm library, increasing the binary size and memory footprint. This flag is a prerequisite for any CLI commands that require file integrity verification or secure password hashing. It depends on the availability of sufficient flash memory and may conflict with memory-constrained builds if not managed alongside other cryptographic modules.
EN_CLI_SHA256.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires secure verification of firmware updates, configuration files, or user authentication via the CLI. Disable it if your project does not perform cryptographic operations to save flash space and reduce the overall memory overhead of the RTOS kernel.

EN_CLI_SHA512.brief: Enables SHA-512 cryptographic hashing support within the caOS Command Line Interface.
EN_CLI_SHA512.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the SHA-512 algorithm library, increasing the binary footprint by approximately 4KB. This flag depends on the core crypto module being enabled. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_SHA512.usage: Enable this flag when the CLI requires secure file integrity verification or password hashing. Disable it if your STM32 device has limited Flash memory and SHA-512 is not required for your specific application to save space.

EN_CLI_SPI.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) support for SPI peripheral debugging and configuration.
EN_CLI_SPI.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the SPI driver hooks for the CLI module. This requires the main CLI module (EN_CLI) to be enabled. If set to 0, all SPI-related diagnostic commands are excluded from the binary, reducing flash memory usage.
EN_CLI_SPI.usage: Enable this flag during the development and integration phase to allow real-time monitoring and manual testing of SPI bus transactions via the serial console. Disable it in production builds to save memory and prevent unauthorized access to hardware registers.

EN_CLI_SSH.brief: Enables or disables the integrated SSH server for the Command Line Interface (CLI) over network.
EN_CLI_SSH.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the SSH daemon and binds it to the network stack; when 0, the service is excluded from the build to save flash memory and RAM. This flag requires the network stack (e.g., lwIP) to be enabled and configured in the project settings.
EN_CLI_SSH.usage: Set to 1 during development or remote maintenance to allow secure shell access to the system console. Set to 0 for production builds where network security is a concern or to reduce the binary footprint if the CLI is only accessed via UART.

EN_CLI_SYSLOG.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) system logging feature for real-time diagnostic output.
EN_CLI_SYSLOG.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS kernel routes internal system events and error logs to the registered CLI output stream. Disabling this (0) reduces CPU overhead and memory usage by preventing string formatting and buffer allocation for logs. This flag depends on the CLI module being initialized in the system startup sequence.
EN_CLI_SYSLOG.usage: Enable this during the development and debugging phase to monitor task switching, stack overflows, or kernel errors via a serial terminal. Disable it in production builds to save flash memory and improve execution performance, as logging operations can introduce latency in time-critical tasks.

EN_CLI_TCP.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) over a TCP/IP network connection.
EN_CLI_TCP.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes a TCP server socket that allows remote access to the system shell. This requires the network stack (LwIP) to be initialized and configured. Disabling this (0) saves memory and reduces CPU overhead by removing the TCP listener task.
EN_CLI_TCP.usage: Enable this during development to debug the system remotely without a physical serial cable. Disable it in production builds to reduce the attack surface and free up system resources.

EN_CLI_TFTP.brief: Enables or disables the built-in TFTP server functionality within the caOS Command Line Interface.
EN_CLI_TFTP.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the TFTP stack to allow remote file transfers over the network. This flag depends on the network stack being active (e.g., LwIP). Disabling it (0) reduces the firmware binary size and frees up RAM used by the TFTP buffer. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_TFTP.usage: Enable this flag when you need to perform remote firmware updates or configuration file uploads/downloads via TFTP. Disable it in production builds if the feature is not required to save memory and reduce the attack surface. Ensure your network interface is correctly initialized before attempting to use the TFTP service.

EN_CLI_TIMER.brief: Enables the internal system timer used for measuring command execution time within the Command Line Interface.
EN_CLI_TIMER.notes: When set to 1, the CLI will track and display the duration of executed commands. This requires the system tick timer to be active. If set to 0, the timing feature is disabled, reducing the memory footprint of the CLI module slightly.
EN_CLI_TIMER.usage: Enable this flag during the development and debugging phase to profile command performance or identify bottlenecks in CLI-based tasks. Disable it in production builds to save minor CPU cycles and memory if command timing is not required by the end user.

EN_CLI_TRACE.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) diagnostic tracing feature for real-time system monitoring.
EN_CLI_TRACE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS outputs internal kernel events and task state transitions to the serial console. Enabling this increases CPU overhead and memory usage for the trace buffer. It requires the UART peripheral to be initialized and is typically disabled in production builds to save resources.
EN_CLI_TRACE.usage: Enable this flag during the debugging phase to track task switching, interrupt latency, or kernel errors. Disable it before final deployment to prevent performance degradation and potential buffer overflows in the trace log.

EN_CLI_UART.brief: Enables the Command Line Interface (CLI) functionality over the UART peripheral.
EN_CLI_UART.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the UART driver and spawns a background task to process serial commands. Disabling this (0) saves RAM and CPU cycles by removing the CLI task and UART interrupt handlers. This flag depends on the UART hardware abstraction layer being correctly configured in the board support package.
EN_CLI_UART.usage: Enable this during development to interact with the system, debug tasks, or monitor variables in real-time via a terminal. Disable it in production builds to reduce the memory footprint and improve security by preventing unauthorized access to system commands.

EN_CLI_UDP_SRV.brief: Enables or disables the built-in UDP Command Line Interface (CLI) server for remote debugging.
EN_CLI_UDP_SRV.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes a UDP socket listener on a predefined port to accept remote commands. This requires the network stack (LwIP) to be initialized and active. If set to 0, the UDP server task is not created, saving RAM and CPU cycles. It depends on EN_NETWORK_STACK being enabled.
EN_CLI_UDP_SRV.usage: Set to 1 during development to allow remote system monitoring and command execution via network tools like Netcat or custom scripts. Set to 0 in production builds to reduce the attack surface and free up system resources. Ensure the network configuration is valid before enabling, otherwise the system may hang during initialization.

EN_CLI_VNC.brief: Enables or disables the VNC server functionality within the CLI interface.
EN_CLI_VNC.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the VNC protocol stack to allow remote graphical interaction via the CLI. When set to 0 (default), the VNC service is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage. This flag depends on the CLI being enabled and requires sufficient heap memory for frame buffer management.
EN_CLI_VNC.usage: Set this to 1 only if your application requires remote GUI access via VNC. If you are developing a headless system or have limited memory, keep this at 0. Ensure that the display driver and frame buffer are correctly initialized using ca_fb_create before starting the VNC service with ca_vnc_service_start.

EN_CLI_WDT.brief: Enables or disables the Command Line Interface (CLI) watchdog timer monitoring.
EN_CLI_WDT.notes: When set to 1, the system monitors the CLI task for responsiveness; if the CLI hangs, the watchdog triggers a system reset. This flag depends on the global watchdog driver being initialized. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_CLI_WDT.usage: Enable this during development to detect if CLI commands are causing task starvation or deadlocks. Disable it during production if the CLI is not required or if you need to perform long-running debug operations that might otherwise trigger a false watchdog reset.

EN_CLI_X25519.brief: Enables the X25519 Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman key exchange protocol within the caOS CLI module.
EN_CLI_X25519.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the cryptographic library required for secure key exchange. Enabling this increases the flash memory footprint by approximately 4KB and requires the system to have sufficient heap space for temporary buffers during the handshake. It depends on the underlying hardware acceleration or software math library being configured in the build system.
EN_CLI_X25519.usage: Enable this flag when the device needs to establish encrypted communication channels or perform secure authentication via the command line interface. Disable it if the device does not require secure remote access or if flash memory constraints are critical. Ensure that the system clock is stable, as cryptographic operations are sensitive to timing.

EN_CRC.brief: Enables hardware-based Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) verification for system memory and task stacks.
EN_CRC.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS performs periodic integrity checks on critical memory areas. This requires the STM32 hardware CRC peripheral to be available and initialized. Disabling this (0) reduces CPU overhead and power consumption but removes the ability to detect silent memory corruption.
EN_CRC.usage: Enable this during development and in safety-critical applications to detect stack overflows or memory corruption caused by hardware faults or pointer errors. Disable only if you are strictly constrained by CPU cycles or if the hardware CRC unit is reserved for other high-priority application tasks.

EN_DAC.brief: Enables the Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) driver support within the caOS RTOS.
EN_DAC.notes: When set to 1, the OS initializes the DAC peripheral hardware abstraction layer. If set to 0, the DAC driver is excluded from the build, reducing binary size. This flag depends on the STM32 hardware having a physical DAC peripheral; enabling it on devices without a DAC will cause compilation or runtime errors.
EN_DAC.usage: Set this to 1 only if your application requires analog signal generation. Disable it (0) to save flash memory and RAM if the DAC is not used in your project. Ensure the corresponding GPIO pins are not being used for other functions when this is enabled.

EN_DHCP_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the automatic Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) client service for network connectivity.
EN_DHCP_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS stack attempts to acquire an IP address from a network router upon startup. If set to 0, the system will rely on a static IP configuration defined in the network settings. This flag requires the TCP/IP stack module to be enabled in the project configuration.
EN_DHCP_SERVICE.usage: Set to 1 when the device needs to operate in a dynamic network environment (like a standard office or home router). Set to 0 if the device requires a fixed IP address for industrial applications or direct peer-to-peer communication. Warning: Disabling this without providing a valid static IP will result in the device being unreachable on the network.

EN_DMA.brief: Enables or disables the Direct Memory Access (DMA) controller support within the caOS RTOS kernel.
EN_DMA.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes and manages DMA channels for peripheral data transfers. Disabling this (0) forces the CPU to handle all data transfers via interrupts or polling, which increases CPU load. This flag must be enabled if any drivers (like UART, SPI, or ADC) are configured to use DMA mode in the hardware abstraction layer.
EN_DMA.usage: Enable this (1) to offload data-heavy tasks from the CPU, improving overall system performance and responsiveness. Disable it (0) only for debugging purposes to isolate potential DMA-related memory corruption or interrupt conflicts, or if the specific STM32 hardware variant lacks DMA support.

EN_DMA2D.brief: Enables or disables the hardware acceleration support for the STM32 DMA2D (Chrom-ART) peripheral.
EN_DMA2D.notes: When set to 1, the ca_dma2d_* API functions are compiled and available for use. When set to 0, these functions are disabled to save code space. This flag is a prerequisite for any graphical operations or memory-to-memory copy tasks that utilize the DMA2D hardware. Ensure your specific STM32 target actually contains a DMA2D peripheral before enabling this.
EN_DMA2D.usage: Set this to 1 if your application requires high-performance image blending, color format conversion, or fast memory filling. If your project does not perform GUI rendering or heavy image processing, keep it at 0 to reduce the binary footprint. If you attempt to call ca_dma2d_init or other related functions while this is 0, the code will fail to compile.

EN_DNS_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the built-in Domain Name System (DNS) client service within the RTOS network stack.
EN_DNS_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the code and memory buffers required to resolve hostnames (e.g., 'example.com') into IP addresses. Disabling this (0) reduces the firmware binary size and saves RAM, but requires the application to use hardcoded IP addresses for all network connections. This flag depends on the network stack being initialized and requires a valid gateway/DNS server configuration in the network settings.
EN_DNS_SERVICE.usage: Enable this flag when your application needs to connect to external servers or cloud services using domain names rather than static IPs. Disable it if your device operates in a closed network with static addressing to conserve system resources. Warning: If disabled, any function call to a DNS resolution service will return an error or fail to compile.

EN_ECDSA_P256.brief: Enables support for ECDSA P-256 cryptographic operations in the caOS library.
EN_ECDSA_P256.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the code for ECDSA P-256 signing, verification, and key generation. This increases the binary size (Flash usage) and requires additional stack space during cryptographic operations. It is a prerequisite for secure boot or TLS features that rely on P-256 certificates. If set to 0, all ca_ecdsa_p256_* functions will be unavailable or return an error.
EN_ECDSA_P256.usage: Enable this flag when your application needs to perform digital signature verification (e.g., verifying firmware updates or secure network handshakes). Disable it if you are constrained by Flash memory and your project does not require P-256 cryptography, or if you are using a different algorithm like Ed25519.

EN_ECDSA_P256_TEST.brief: Enables or disables the inclusion of ECDSA P-256 cryptographic test vectors and self-test routines.
EN_ECDSA_P256_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the system includes additional code for verifying ECDSA P-256 operations using predefined test vectors. This increases the binary size (Flash usage). It is typically used during development or factory validation. It depends on the availability of the ECDSA P-256 module in the caOS build.
EN_ECDSA_P256_TEST.usage: Set to 1 only during the debugging or validation phase of the security stack to ensure the ECDSA implementation is functioning correctly. Set to 0 for production builds to save Flash memory and prevent potential side-channel exposure of test routines. Use ca_ecdsa_p256_selftest to trigger the verification if enabled.

EN_ED25519.brief: Enables hardware-accelerated or software-based ED25519 digital signature verification within the RTOS kernel.
EN_ED25519.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the ED25519 cryptographic library in the build, increasing the binary size and RAM usage. It requires a sufficient stack size for the task performing the verification. If set to 0, all related cryptographic functions will be unavailable, and calls to them will result in a compilation error or a linker failure.
EN_ED25519.usage: Enable this flag when your application needs to verify secure boot signatures, firmware updates, or encrypted communication packets. Only enable it if your STM32 device has enough Flash and RAM to accommodate the library; otherwise, you may encounter stack overflows or memory allocation failures.

EN_ED25519_TEST.brief: Enables the inclusion of the ED25519 cryptographic test suite within the caOS kernel build.
EN_ED25519_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the system compiles and links the ED25519 verification unit tests. This increases the total flash memory footprint significantly. It depends on the core cryptographic library being enabled. Typical values are 0 for production builds and 1 for development or hardware validation phases.
EN_ED25519_TEST.usage: Enable this flag only during the bring-up phase or when performing security regression testing on new hardware. Do not enable this in production firmware, as it consumes unnecessary flash space and exposes test entry points that are not required for standard application operation.

EN_ETH.brief: Enables or disables the Ethernet peripheral driver stack within the caOS RTOS.
EN_ETH.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the Ethernet MAC/PHY hardware and includes the TCP/IP stack tasks. When set to 0, the Ethernet driver is excluded from the build, reducing flash and RAM usage. This flag requires the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) for the specific STM32 Ethernet peripheral to be correctly configured in the project settings.
EN_ETH.usage: Set this to 1 if your application requires network connectivity (e.g., LwIP, web server, or socket communication). Set to 0 if the project does not use networking to save memory resources. Warning: Disabling this while other tasks attempt to call network-related APIs will result in compilation errors or runtime crashes.

EN_ETH_CHK_HW.brief: Enables hardware-level integrity checks for the Ethernet peripheral controller.
EN_ETH_CHK_HW.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS performs periodic register validation and status monitoring of the Ethernet MAC/DMA hardware. Disabling this (0) reduces CPU overhead but removes automatic detection of hardware hangs or peripheral clock failures. It depends on the Ethernet driver being initialized and requires the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) to support status polling.
EN_ETH_CHK_HW.usage: Enable this during development and production to ensure the network interface remains responsive. Change to 0 only if you are experiencing extreme CPU constraints and have implemented custom, lightweight monitoring, or if the hardware design does not support status register polling.

EN_ETH_DBG.brief: Enables or disables the Ethernet peripheral debugging and diagnostic logging features within the caOS kernel.
EN_ETH_DBG.notes: When set to 1, the system routes Ethernet driver status messages and packet statistics to the configured debug UART or ITM port. Enabling this increases CPU overhead and memory usage for the logging buffer. It depends on the global 'EN_DEBUG' flag being enabled. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_ETH_DBG.usage: Enable this flag during the development phase when troubleshooting network connectivity issues, dropped packets, or PHY initialization failures. Disable it in production builds to save flash memory, reduce RAM usage, and prevent potential timing issues caused by logging latency.

EN_EVENT.brief: Enables the event flag management system within the caOS kernel.
EN_EVENT.notes: When set to 1, the kernel includes code for event group synchronization primitives. Disabling it (0) reduces the kernel binary size and RAM usage by removing event-related structures. This flag is a prerequisite for using os_event_wait and os_event_set functions.
EN_EVENT.usage: Enable this flag if your application requires tasks to synchronize based on multiple event signals or flags. Keep it disabled if your project only uses simple semaphores or mutexes to save memory on resource-constrained STM32 devices.

EN_EXTI.brief: Enables the caOS external interrupt (EXTI) management layer for handling hardware signals.
EN_EXTI.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS hooks into the STM32 EXTI controller to manage ISRs; when 0, the RTOS ignores external interrupts, requiring manual implementation. This flag depends on the HAL_EXTI_MODULE_ENABLED definition in the STM32 HAL configuration.
EN_EXTI.usage: Enable this when your application needs to trigger tasks or semaphores based on physical pin transitions (e.g., buttons, sensors). Disable it only if you are implementing custom interrupt handlers outside the RTOS framework to save memory or avoid conflicts with legacy code.

EN_FAT.brief: Enables the integrated FAT file system support within the caOS kernel.
EN_FAT.notes: When set to 1, the kernel includes the FAT driver stack, increasing Flash and RAM usage. It requires the hardware abstraction layer for SD/MMC or SPI-Flash to be configured. If set to 0, all file system related APIs will be disabled, reducing the binary footprint.
EN_FAT.usage: Enable this flag only when your application needs to read or write files to external storage media. Ensure that the underlying peripheral drivers are initialized before calling any file system functions to avoid hard faults.

EN_FAT_CRYPT.brief: Enables or disables the integrated hardware-accelerated encryption layer for the FAT file system.
EN_FAT_CRYPT.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS automatically encrypts/decrypts data blocks during SD card or Flash read/write operations. Enabling this requires the 'EN_CRYPTO_LIB' flag to be active and increases CPU overhead by approximately 5-8%. It is incompatible with standard FAT32 drivers that do not support encrypted sectors.
EN_FAT_CRYPT.usage: Set to 1 when storing sensitive user data or configuration files on external storage media to ensure data privacy. Disable it (0) if you are experiencing performance bottlenecks during heavy file I/O or if the storage medium is not intended to hold confidential information.

EN_FAT_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the integrated FAT file system service layer within caOS.
EN_FAT_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the FAT file system driver and allocates the necessary memory buffers for file operations. Disabling this (0) reduces the kernel's memory footprint and removes dependencies on SD card or Flash storage drivers. This flag must be enabled if your application uses the 'ca_fs_open' or 'ca_fs_write' APIs.
EN_FAT_SERVICE.usage: Enable this flag only if your project requires reading or writing files to external storage media. If your application is strictly memory-based or uses raw peripheral access, keep this disabled to save RAM and Flash space. Ensure that the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) for your storage interface (e.g., SPI or SDMMC) is correctly configured before enabling this service.

EN_FB.brief: Enables or disables the Framebuffer (FB) subsystem in caOS.
EN_FB.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes and manages framebuffer memory and associated drawing primitives. When set to 0 (default), the framebuffer module is excluded from the build, reducing binary size and RAM usage. This flag is a prerequisite for using any ca_fb_* API functions. If disabled, calling ca_fb_* functions will result in linker errors.
EN_FB.usage: Change this value to 1 only if your application requires graphical output or pixel-level manipulation using the ca_fb_* API. If your project does not use a display or graphical interface, keep it at 0 to save system resources. Ensure that your hardware configuration supports the required memory allocation for the framebuffer before enabling.

EN_FLASH.brief: Enables or disables the internal Flash memory driver and management services within caOS.
EN_FLASH.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the Flash abstraction layer, allowing tasks to perform read/write operations on non-volatile memory. Disabling this (0) reduces the kernel's memory footprint and removes dependencies on the STM32 HAL Flash drivers. This flag must be enabled if your application uses the caOS File System or persistent configuration storage.
EN_FLASH.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires saving persistent data or logs to the internal Flash. Disable it if you are optimizing for minimal code size or if your hardware design does not require Flash access, as this prevents potential bus contention or accidental memory corruption during runtime.

EN_FMAC.brief: Enables the hardware support for the STM32 Filter Math Accelerator (FMAC).
