EN_FMAC.notes: When set to 1, the caOS kernel initializes and includes the driver for the FMAC peripheral. This allows the system to offload complex mathematical operations like FIR/IIR filtering to dedicated hardware. Disabling this (0) saves code space and memory but forces all filtering operations to be performed by the CPU, which may significantly increase processing time. This flag requires the target STM32 MCU to have an integrated FMAC peripheral.
EN_FMAC.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires high-performance digital signal processing (DSP) or audio filtering. If your project does not perform real-time signal processing, keep this disabled to minimize the memory footprint. Ensure your hardware supports the FMAC peripheral before enabling, otherwise, the system may trigger a hardware fault during initialization.

EN_HASH.brief: Enables the internal hash-based integrity check for task control blocks and system structures.
EN_HASH.notes: When set to 1, the kernel calculates a checksum for critical memory regions to detect corruption. Enabling this increases CPU overhead per context switch and requires additional RAM for storage. It depends on the system's memory protection unit (MPU) configuration being active.
EN_HASH.usage: Enable this during the development and debugging phase to catch stack overflows or illegal memory writes. Disable it in final production builds if the CPU cycles are strictly limited and the system has passed extensive stability testing, as it adds a slight latency to task scheduling.

EN_HTTPS_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the HTTPS server functionality in the caOS network stack.
EN_HTTPS_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the system compiles and includes the HTTPS service code, allowing secure web communication. This flag depends on the underlying TLS/SSL library support within caOS. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled). Enabling this increases the binary size and memory footprint significantly due to cryptographic overhead.
EN_HTTPS_SERVICE.usage: Set this to 1 only if your application requires secure web services (HTTPS). If your device only uses plain HTTP or does not act as a web server, set this to 0 to save flash memory and RAM. Ensure that your hardware has sufficient resources to handle the computational load of TLS handshakes.

EN_HTTP_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the built-in HTTP server service within the caOS RTOS.
EN_HTTP_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the network stack and starts the HTTP server task. When set to 0, the service is excluded from the build, reducing flash and RAM usage. This flag requires the TCP/IP stack (e.g., LwIP) to be enabled in the project configuration.
EN_HTTP_SERVICE.usage: Set to 1 if your application requires a web interface for remote monitoring or configuration. Set to 0 if the device does not need network connectivity or if you are optimizing for minimal memory footprint. Ensure that the network interface hardware is initialized before this service starts to avoid runtime errors.

EN_I2C.brief: Enables or disables the I2C communication driver stack within the caOS RTOS.
EN_I2C.notes: When set to 1, the I2C peripheral drivers and associated interrupt handlers are compiled into the kernel. When set to 0, the I2C stack is excluded, reducing the total flash memory footprint. This flag is a prerequisite for any I2C-based peripheral drivers (e.g., sensors, EEPROMs) to function.
EN_I2C.usage: Set this to 1 if your project requires communication with I2C devices. Set to 0 if your hardware design does not use I2C to save memory. Ensure that the corresponding hardware pins are correctly configured in the STM32CubeMX project before enabling this flag.

EN_IPERF_SERVICE.brief: Enables the integrated network performance testing service (iPerf) within the RTOS stack.
EN_IPERF_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the system allocates a dedicated task and memory buffer for iPerf server functionality. This flag depends on the TCP/IP stack being initialized and active. Disabling it (0) saves approximately 4KB of RAM and reduces CPU overhead during network idle states.
EN_IPERF_SERVICE.usage: Enable this during the development and QA phases to benchmark network throughput and verify stack stability. It must be set to 0 in production firmware to prevent unauthorized network testing and to minimize the memory footprint.

EN_IP_DEFRAG.brief: Enables the built-in IP packet fragmentation reassembly module in the caOS network stack.
EN_IP_DEFRAG.notes: When enabled (1), the system allocates a buffer pool to reconstruct fragmented IP packets before passing them to the application layer. Disabling (0) saves significant RAM but causes the stack to drop any incoming fragmented packets. This flag depends on the network stack being initialized and requires sufficient heap memory to hold the reassembly buffers.
EN_IP_DEFRAG.usage: Enable this if your device communicates over networks where MTU sizes vary or packets are frequently fragmented. Disable it to conserve RAM in memory-constrained systems if you are certain that all incoming traffic will arrive as single, non-fragmented packets.

EN_IP_FRAG.brief: Enables the IP fragmentation support module in the caOS network stack.
EN_IP_FRAG.notes: When set to 1, the system can reassemble incoming fragmented IP packets and fragment outgoing packets that exceed the MTU. This flag is a prerequisite for the ca_ip_defrag_* and ca_ip_frag_* API functions. Disabling this (0) reduces memory usage by removing the reassembly buffer but prevents communication with devices that send fragmented packets.
EN_IP_FRAG.usage: Enable this if your device needs to communicate over networks where packet fragmentation is common (e.g., certain VPNs or complex routed networks). If your device only communicates over a local, controlled network with a fixed MTU, you may disable it to save RAM. Warning: If disabled, fragmented packets will be dropped, potentially causing connection timeouts or data loss.

EN_JPEG.brief: Enables or disables the JPEG hardware acceleration and processing library support.
EN_JPEG.notes: When set to 1, the ca_jpeg_* API functions are compiled into the binary. When set to 0, these functions are excluded, reducing the total flash memory footprint. This flag has no direct dependencies on other OS flags but is required if your application intends to use the ca_jpeg_decode or ca_jpeg_encode functions.
EN_JPEG.usage: Change this value to 1 only if your project requires image processing or compression/decompression of JPEG streams. If your application does not perform image manipulation, keep this at 0 to save valuable flash space. Warning: Enabling this without sufficient memory or hardware support on the target STM32 chip may lead to compilation errors or runtime faults.

EN_KEYSTORE_SERVICE.brief: Enables the secure keystore service for managing cryptographic keys and sensitive credentials within the RTOS.
EN_KEYSTORE_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the secure storage driver and allocates memory for the keystore manager. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) supporting secure flash or EEPROM access. If disabled (0), any calls to keystore APIs will return an error code or trigger a hard fault.
EN_KEYSTORE_SERVICE.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires encrypted storage for keys, certificates, or sensitive configuration data. Change this to 0 only if your project does not use cryptography or if you are optimizing for minimal memory footprint on devices without secure storage hardware. Ensure that the underlying hardware memory protection unit (MPU) is configured correctly before enabling this service.

EN_KEYS_STORE.brief: Enables the internal persistent storage mechanism for system-wide key-value pairs.
EN_KEYS_STORE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS allocates a dedicated memory block for storing configuration keys. Disabling this (0) removes the storage API from the build, reducing flash and RAM usage. It depends on the underlying HAL flash driver being initialized. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_KEYS_STORE.usage: Enable this when your application needs to save settings like calibration data, network credentials, or user preferences across power cycles. Change to 0 only if your application does not require persistent storage to save memory resources. Warning: Ensure the flash memory sector defined for this store is not being used by your application code or bootloader to prevent data corruption.

EN_LED.brief: Enables or disables the built-in LED heartbeat and status indicator functionality within the RTOS.
EN_LED.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS kernel will periodically toggle the designated system LED to indicate that the scheduler is running. If set to 0, the LED driver code is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage. This flag requires the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) to have a valid GPIO pin defined for the system LED in the board support package.
EN_LED.usage: Enable this during initial board bring-up or debugging to verify that the RTOS kernel is alive and not stuck in a hard fault. Disable it in production builds to save power and free up the GPIO pin for other application-specific tasks.

EN_LITTLE_E.brief: Defines the system endianness as Little-Endian when set to 1.
EN_LITTLE_E.notes: When enabled (1), the processor stores the least significant byte at the lowest memory address. This is the native mode for ARM Cortex-M processors used in STM32. Disabling this (0) would force Big-Endian mode, which is generally not supported by standard STM32 hardware and would cause severe data corruption and system crashes.
EN_LITTLE_E.usage: This flag should almost always remain set to 1 for STM32 development. Change this only if you are porting the RTOS to a specific architecture that requires Big-Endian byte ordering. Incorrectly setting this to 0 will result in incorrect integer arithmetic, pointer errors, and failure of communication protocols like SPI or I2C.

EN_LPTIM.brief: Enables the Low-Power Timer (LPTIM) peripheral support within the caOS kernel.
EN_LPTIM.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS utilizes the LPTIM hardware for low-power tick generation and sleep mode wake-ups. Disabling this (0) forces the system to use standard timers, which may increase power consumption during idle states. This flag requires the STM32 LPTIM peripheral to be physically present on the MCU and correctly initialized in the hardware abstraction layer.
EN_LPTIM.usage: Enable this flag when designing battery-powered applications that require the system to remain in Stop mode while maintaining timekeeping. Change to 0 only if you are debugging power issues or if the specific STM32 variant lacks an LPTIM peripheral. Incorrect configuration may lead to system hangs or failure to wake from low-power modes.

EN_LPUART.brief: Enables or disables the Low Power UART (LPUART) peripheral driver support within the caOS kernel.
EN_LPUART.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes and manages the LPUART hardware for low-power serial communication. When set to 0, the driver is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage. This flag depends on the STM32 hardware having an LPUART peripheral available; enabling it on chips without LPUART will cause compilation errors.
EN_LPUART.usage: Set to 1 if your application requires serial communication while the MCU is in Stop mode to wake up the system. Set to 0 if you are using standard UART peripherals or do not require serial communication, as this saves memory and prevents unnecessary hardware initialization.

EN_MDNS_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the built-in mDNS (Multicast DNS) service for network device discovery.
EN_MDNS_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes a background task to broadcast the device's hostname and IP address on the local network. This requires the TCP/IP stack (e.g., LwIP) to be active and configured. Disabling this (0) reduces memory usage and CPU overhead by removing the mDNS responder task.
EN_MDNS_SERVICE.usage: Enable this when you want your device to be reachable via a friendly hostname (e.g., 'device.local') instead of a static IP address. Disable it if you are operating in a strictly controlled network environment where multicast traffic is prohibited or if you need to save RAM/Flash resources.

EN_MEASURE.brief: Enables the internal CPU load and execution time measurement module for system tasks.
EN_MEASURE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS tracks task execution time and idle percentage. This requires additional RAM for storage and slightly increases context switch overhead. It depends on the hardware timer configured in the HAL layer. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_MEASURE.usage: Enable this during the development and profiling phase to identify bottlenecks or verify task timing requirements. Disable it in the final production firmware to save CPU cycles and reduce memory footprint.

EN_MESSAGE.brief: Enables the inter-task messaging system (mailboxes/queues) within the caOS kernel.
EN_MESSAGE.notes: When set to 1, the kernel allocates memory and initializes structures for message passing. Disabling this (0) reduces the static RAM footprint and code size significantly. This flag is a prerequisite for using any OS_Send or OS_Receive functions; if disabled, calling these functions will result in a compile-time error or a kernel panic.
EN_MESSAGE.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires tasks to exchange data or synchronize via messages. Disable it only in extremely memory-constrained systems where tasks operate in complete isolation to save precious SRAM and Flash space.

EN_MODBUS_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the integrated Modbus RTU/TCP communication service within the caOS kernel.
EN_MODBUS_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS allocates memory for the Modbus task and initializes the protocol stack. When set to 0, the service is excluded from the build, reducing Flash and RAM usage. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) having the necessary UART or Ethernet drivers configured.
EN_MODBUS_SERVICE.usage: Set to 1 if your application requires Modbus communication for industrial sensors or PLC integration. Set to 0 to save system resources if the project does not use Modbus. Ensure that the associated communication peripheral is not being used by another task if this flag is enabled to avoid resource conflicts.

EN_MQTT_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the integrated MQTT client service within the caOS RTOS stack.
EN_MQTT_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the MQTT task and associated network buffers are initialized during system boot. Disabling this (0) reduces the overall RAM footprint and flash usage by excluding the MQTT protocol stack. This flag depends on the network stack being enabled (e.g., EN_LWIP_STACK must be 1).
EN_MQTT_SERVICE.usage: Set to 1 if your application requires remote telemetry or cloud connectivity via MQTT. Set to 0 if the device operates in a standalone mode or uses a different communication protocol to save system resources. Ensure your heap size is sufficient before enabling, as the MQTT client requires dynamic memory allocation for message buffers.

EN_NET.brief: Enables the integrated networking stack and TCP/IP protocol support within the caOS RTOS.
EN_NET.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes the network interface drivers and allocates memory for the socket buffer pool. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) having Ethernet or Wi-Fi peripherals configured. If set to 0, all network-related tasks and memory allocations are excluded from the build, reducing the total flash and RAM footprint.
EN_NET.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires network connectivity (e.g., MQTT, HTTP, or socket communication). Disable it for low-power or resource-constrained applications that do not require connectivity to save memory. Ensure that the network buffer size is also configured in the corresponding header file if this flag is enabled, otherwise, the system may trigger a hard fault during initialization.

EN_NET_DHCP.brief: Enables the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) client module for automatic IP address assignment.
EN_NET_DHCP.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS stack attempts to negotiate network settings with a DHCP server upon initialization. If set to 0, the system defaults to a static IP configuration defined in the network settings. This flag requires the TCP/IP stack (e.g., LwIP) to be enabled in the project configuration.
EN_NET_DHCP.usage: Enable this when the device needs to connect to networks where IP addresses are managed by a router or server. Disable it for industrial or point-to-point applications where a fixed, predictable IP address is required to prevent connection delays during boot-up.

EN_NET_DNS.brief: Enables or disables the Domain Name System (DNS) client functionality within the caOS networking stack.
EN_NET_DNS.notes: When set to 1, the system includes code to resolve human-readable hostnames (e.g., 'example.com') into IP addresses. When set to 0, the DNS client is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage. This flag depends on the TCP/IP stack being enabled; if the network stack is disabled, this flag must also be 0.
EN_NET_DNS.usage: Enable this (1) if your application needs to connect to remote servers using URLs instead of hardcoded IP addresses. Disable it (0) to save memory if your device only communicates via static IP addresses or if you are performing manual IP resolution.

EN_NET_FILTER.brief: Enables hardware-level packet filtering for network traffic
EN_NET_FILTER.notes: When set to 1, incoming network packets are filtered at hardware level before reaching the OS network stack, reducing CPU overhead. When set to 0, all packets bypass hardware filtering and go directly to software processing. This flag requires the network hardware to support filtering and depends on proper MAC address configuration. Hardware filtering is typically only available on certain STM32 Ethernet peripherals.
EN_NET_FILTER.usage: Set to 1 when implementing security policies or reducing network processing overhead in production systems. Set to 0 for debugging network issues or when hardware doesn't support filtering. Warning: Setting to 1 on unsupported hardware may cause network initialization failures or packet loss. Only enable if your STM32 device has hardware filtering capabilities.

EN_NET_MDNS.brief: Enables or disables the multicast DNS (mDNS) service discovery protocol within the caOS network stack.
EN_NET_MDNS.notes: When set to 1, the system announces its hostname and services on the local network, allowing other devices to resolve its IP address via 'hostname.local'. Disabling this (0) reduces memory footprint and CPU overhead by removing the mDNS responder task and associated UDP socket handling. This flag requires the TCP/IP stack to be initialized and typically depends on the EN_NET_UDP flag being enabled.
EN_NET_MDNS.usage: Enable this when you want your device to be discoverable by other network clients without needing a static IP or a central DNS server. Disable it in resource-constrained applications where network discovery is not required or to minimize the attack surface of the device on the local network.

EN_NET_NTP.brief: Enables or disables the Network Time Protocol (NTP) client service within the caOS RTOS stack.
EN_NET_NTP.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the NTP client task to synchronize the internal RTC with external time servers. This flag depends on the network stack being active (EN_NET_STACK must be 1). If disabled, the system will not attempt to fetch network time, and the RTC will rely solely on manual setting or hardware battery backup.
EN_NET_NTP.usage: Enable this when your application requires accurate, synchronized timestamps for logging or scheduling. Change to 0 if your device operates in an isolated network or if you want to reduce memory footprint and network traffic. Warning: Ensure your network gateway and DNS settings are correctly configured before enabling, otherwise the task may hang waiting for a response.

EN_NET_SYSLOG.brief: Enables or disables the system-wide logging of network events to a remote syslog server.
EN_NET_SYSLOG.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS will forward internal network stack events and error messages to a configured UDP syslog server. This feature requires the network stack (TCP/IP) to be initialized and active. Disabling this (0) reduces CPU overhead and memory usage by removing the logging task and buffer allocations.
EN_NET_SYSLOG.usage: Enable this during the development and debugging phase to monitor network connectivity issues or stack errors in real-time. Disable it in production builds to save system resources and prevent unnecessary network traffic. Ensure the syslog server IP is correctly configured in the network settings before enabling this flag.

EN_NOTIFY.brief: Enables the Task Notification feature, allowing tasks to send lightweight signals or data directly to other tasks.
EN_NOTIFY.notes: When set to 1, the OS allocates a notification value and state variable for every task control block. This increases RAM usage per task. It is a prerequisite for using functions like os_task_notify() and os_task_wait_notify(). If set to 0, these functions will be disabled, and the kernel will ignore any notification-related calls.
EN_NOTIFY.usage: Enable this when you need a fast, low-overhead alternative to semaphores or queues for simple task synchronization or event signaling. Change this to 0 only if you are extremely constrained on RAM and are certain your application does not require direct task-to-task signaling.

EN_NTP_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the built-in Network Time Protocol (NTP) client service for automatic system clock synchronization.
EN_NTP_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes a background task to periodically query a time server; when set to 0, the service is excluded from the build, reducing flash and RAM usage. This flag requires the TCP/IP stack (e.g., LwIP) to be enabled and a valid network interface to be active.
EN_NTP_SERVICE.usage: Enable this when your application requires accurate UTC timestamps or logging with real-world time. Disable it if your device operates in an isolated network without internet access or if you are using an external Hardware Real-Time Clock (RTC) module to save system resources.

EN_PACKET_TRACER.brief: Enables the internal diagnostic logging system for tracking inter-task communication packets.
EN_PACKET_TRACER.notes: When set to 1, the kernel records metadata for every message queue and mailbox transaction. Enabling this increases CPU overhead and RAM usage for the trace buffer. It depends on the OS_DEBUG_LEVEL being set to at least 1. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_PACKET_TRACER.usage: Enable this flag during the development and debugging phase to trace message flow and identify race conditions or lost packets. Disable it in production builds to save memory and improve system performance, as the tracing mechanism consumes significant clock cycles.

EN_POOL.brief: Enables the dynamic memory pool management system within caOS.
EN_POOL.notes: When set to 1, the kernel allocates memory from pre-defined fixed-size pools instead of using the standard heap. This prevents memory fragmentation and ensures deterministic allocation times. Disabling this (0) forces the system to rely on standard heap allocation, which may be slower and prone to fragmentation. This flag must be enabled if your application uses message queues or dynamic task creation.
EN_POOL.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires frequent creation and deletion of objects like tasks or messages. Change this to 0 only if your system is strictly static and you need to save the small amount of RAM overhead required for the pool management structures. Ensure that the pool sizes defined in the configuration are sufficient for your peak load to avoid allocation failures.

EN_PWR.brief: Enables the power management module for the caOS RTOS.
EN_PWR.notes: When set to 1, the kernel enters low-power sleep modes during idle time. When set to 0, the CPU remains in active mode continuously. This flag requires the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) to have tickless idle support configured. Typical values are 0 for debugging and 1 for battery-powered applications.
EN_PWR.usage: Enable this flag when your device needs to minimize power consumption during periods of inactivity. Disable it if you experience issues with peripheral wake-up latency or if you are using a debugger that loses connection when the CPU enters sleep mode.

EN_PWR_DBG.brief: Enables or disables the power management debug logging features within the RTOS kernel.
EN_PWR_DBG.notes: When set to 1, the system outputs detailed power state transitions and sleep mode entry/exit logs to the debug console. Disabling it (0) reduces CPU overhead and memory footprint. This flag depends on the global debug logging system being active; if the main logging module is disabled, this flag has no effect.
EN_PWR_DBG.usage: Set to 1 during the development phase when troubleshooting battery life issues or unexpected wake-up events. Set to 0 for production builds to minimize power consumption and prevent UART/ITM buffer overflows caused by excessive logging.

EN_PYTHON.brief: Enables or disables the Python scripting engine integration within the caOS RTOS.
EN_PYTHON.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the Python interpreter and related API (e.g., ca_python_start). This significantly increases the memory footprint (RAM and Flash) and requires a larger stack size for tasks running Python scripts. When set to 0, the Python module is excluded from the build, reducing binary size and memory usage. This flag is independent of other modules but is required if you intend to use any ca_python_* functions.
EN_PYTHON.usage: Set to 1 only if your application requires dynamic scripting capabilities or Python-based automation. For standard embedded control tasks where performance and memory efficiency are critical, keep this set to 0. If you attempt to call ca_python_start while this is 0, the linker will report an undefined reference error.

EN_QSPI.brief: Enables or disables the Quad-SPI (QSPI) peripheral driver support within the caOS kernel.
EN_QSPI.notes: When set to 1, the OS initializes the QSPI controller and includes the necessary HAL drivers for external flash memory access. When set to 0, the QSPI peripheral is ignored, reducing the kernel binary size and freeing up memory. This flag must be enabled if your hardware design uses an external QSPI flash chip for data storage or XIP (Execute-in-Place) operations.
EN_QSPI.usage: Set this to 1 only if your specific STM32 board has an external QSPI flash memory connected. If you attempt to use QSPI functions while this is set to 0, the system will trigger a hard fault or return null pointers. Keep it at 0 for projects that do not require external memory to save precious RAM and Flash resources.

EN_RNG.brief: Enables the hardware random number generator (RNG) peripheral driver within the caOS kernel.
EN_RNG.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes the STM32 RNG peripheral and provides a thread-safe API for entropy generation. Disabling this (0) reduces the memory footprint and removes the dependency on the RNG hardware clock. This flag requires the STM32 RNG peripheral to be present on the specific MCU model.
EN_RNG.usage: Enable this when your application requires cryptographically secure random numbers, unique session IDs, or jitter for network protocols. Change to 0 if you need to save power or if the RNG peripheral is not available on your target hardware. Warning: Ensure the RNG clock is enabled in the system clock configuration, otherwise the kernel may hang during initialization.

EN_ROUTE_SERVICE.brief: Enables the internal routing service for inter-task communication and message passing.
EN_ROUTE_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes the routing table and message buffers. Disabling this (0) reduces RAM usage by approximately 2KB but prevents tasks from using the OS_Route_Send() and OS_Route_Receive() APIs. This flag must be enabled if any system modules rely on asynchronous event signaling.
EN_ROUTE_SERVICE.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires decoupled communication between tasks. Disable it only in extremely memory-constrained systems where all task synchronization is handled strictly via binary semaphores or direct task notifications to save stack and heap space.

EN_RTC.brief: Enables the Real-Time Clock (RTC) driver integration within the caOS kernel.
EN_RTC.notes: When set to 1, the OS initializes the hardware RTC peripheral and provides system-wide timekeeping services. If set to 0, all RTC-related API calls will return an error or remain unimplemented. This flag depends on the underlying STM32 HAL RTC configuration being correctly defined in the project's hardware abstraction layer.
EN_RTC.usage: Set to 1 if your application requires timestamping, scheduling based on wall-clock time, or low-power wake-up alarms. Disable it (0) to save flash memory and reduce initialization time if the application does not require time-tracking features.

EN_RWLOCK.brief: Enables or disables the Read-Write Lock (RWLock) synchronization primitive in the caOS kernel.
EN_RWLOCK.notes: When set to 1, the kernel includes code for RWLock objects, allowing multiple readers or a single writer to access a resource. Disabling this (0) reduces the kernel binary size and memory footprint. This flag has no dependencies on other synchronization primitives but is required if any application task attempts to initialize or use an RWLock handle.
EN_RWLOCK.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires high-concurrency access to shared resources where read operations significantly outnumber write operations. Change to 0 if your project is memory-constrained and does not utilize RWLocks to save flash and RAM. Warning: disabling this while the application code still references RWLock functions will result in compilation errors.

EN_SAI.brief: Enables the Serial Audio Interface (SAI) peripheral driver support in caOS.
EN_SAI.notes: When set to 1, the caOS SAI driver module is compiled and initialized, allowing the use of ca_sai_* API functions. This flag consumes additional flash memory and requires the corresponding hardware peripheral to be available on the STM32 chip. If set to 0, any attempt to call ca_sai_* functions will result in a compilation error or linker failure.
EN_SAI.usage: Enable this flag only when your application requires digital audio streaming (e.g., I2S, TDM, or PDM audio interfaces). If your project does not use audio peripherals, keep this set to 0 to save system resources and reduce the binary footprint.

EN_SDIO.brief: Enables the SDIO peripheral driver for SD card communication within the caOS RTOS.
EN_SDIO.notes: When set to 1, the OS initializes the SDIO hardware abstraction layer and includes the SD card file system support. Disabling this (0) reduces the binary footprint and frees up CPU cycles if no SD card is used. This flag depends on the hardware having an SDIO interface connected; if enabled without physical hardware, the system may hang during the initialization phase.
EN_SDIO.usage: Set this to 1 when your application requires logging data to an SD card or loading configuration files from external storage. Change to 0 if you are using a different storage medium (like SPI Flash) or if the SDIO pins are needed for other GPIO functions to prevent hardware conflicts.

EN_SHA256.brief: Enables the SHA-256 cryptographic hash function implementation in the RTOS kernel
EN_SHA256.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS includes SHA-256 hashing capabilities which increases binary size by approximately 2-4KB and requires cryptographic hardware support on STM32 devices. Setting to 0 removes all SHA-256 functionality and will cause linker errors if any application code attempts to use these functions. The flag depends on EN_CRYPTO being enabled for hardware acceleration support.
EN_SHA256.usage: Enable this flag when implementing secure communication protocols, firmware verification, or digital signature validation. Disable only when memory constraints are critical and no cryptographic hashing is required. Warning: Disabling this flag while code references SHA-256 functions will cause compilation failures

EN_SHA256_TEST.brief: Enables or disables the built-in SHA-256 cryptographic integrity verification suite for system binaries.
EN_SHA256_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS performs a checksum validation of the application image during the boot sequence. This requires the hardware CRC or cryptographic acceleration unit to be initialized. If set to 0, the boot time is reduced, but the system loses the ability to detect unauthorized firmware modifications or memory corruption at startup.
EN_SHA256_TEST.usage: Enable this flag during production builds to ensure firmware authenticity and integrity. Disable it only during early development stages if you need to speed up the flashing and boot cycle, or if you are using a custom bootloader that handles verification externally. Ensure that your linker script reserves space for the checksum signature if this is enabled.

EN_SHA512.brief: Enables or disables the hardware-accelerated SHA-512 cryptographic hashing module within the RTOS kernel.
EN_SHA512.notes: When set to 1, the kernel includes SHA-512 support, increasing the binary size and memory footprint. It requires the underlying STM32 hardware to have a functional HASH peripheral. If set to 0, any calls to SHA-512 functions will return an error or trigger a linker error if the code is not wrapped in preprocessor checks.
EN_SHA512.usage: Enable this flag only if your application requires secure hashing, data integrity checks, or digital signature verification. Disable it to save flash memory and RAM if your project does not utilize SHA-512, as it consumes significant system resources.

EN_SHA512_TEST.brief: Enables the built-in SHA-512 cryptographic integrity verification test suite during system startup.
EN_SHA512_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS executes a self-test routine on the SHA-512 hardware accelerator or software library before the scheduler starts. If set to 0, the test is skipped, reducing boot time. This flag depends on the availability of the cryptographic module in the current STM32 target and requires sufficient stack space for the test execution.
EN_SHA512_TEST.usage: Enable this during the development and production validation phases to ensure the integrity of the hashing engine. Disable it only in final production builds if boot time requirements are extremely strict and the hardware has been verified to be reliable across all units.

EN_SPDIFRX.brief: Enables or disables the SPDIFRX peripheral driver support in caOS.
EN_SPDIFRX.notes: When set to 1, the caOS SPDIFRX driver (ca_spdifrx_*) is compiled into the binary, allowing the application to interface with the hardware SPDIF receiver. When set to 0, the driver is excluded, reducing flash memory usage. This flag does not have direct dependencies on other peripherals but requires the target STM32 MCU to have a physical SPDIFRX peripheral.
EN_SPDIFRX.usage: Set this to 1 only if your application needs to receive digital audio data via the SPDIF interface. If your project does not use SPDIFRX, keep it at 0 to save code space and avoid unnecessary peripheral initialization code.

EN_SPI.brief: Enables or disables the SPI peripheral driver support within the caOS RTOS kernel.
EN_SPI.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes SPI hardware abstraction layers and allocates memory for SPI-related structures. When set to 0, all SPI-related code is excluded from the build, reducing the final binary size. This flag is a prerequisite for any SPI-based communication tasks; if disabled, calls to SPI functions will result in compilation errors or undefined behavior.
EN_SPI.usage: Set this to 1 only if your application requires SPI communication (e.g., interfacing with sensors, displays, or external memory). Keep it at 0 if your project does not use SPI to save flash memory and RAM. Ensure that the corresponding hardware pins are correctly configured in your STM32CubeMX project if you enable this flag.

EN_SPI_DMA.brief: Enables Direct Memory Access (DMA) support for SPI peripheral communication.
EN_SPI_DMA.notes: When set to 1, SPI data transfers bypass the CPU, reducing overhead. When set to 0, the system uses standard interrupt-driven or polling methods. This flag requires the corresponding DMA controller clock to be enabled in the system initialization code. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_SPI_DMA.usage: Enable this when your application requires high-speed SPI data transfers or when the CPU is heavily loaded with other tasks. Change to 0 only if you are debugging SPI timing issues or if the specific STM32 hardware configuration lacks DMA support for the chosen SPI instance.

EN_SSH_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the integrated SSH server service within the caOS RTOS kernel.
EN_SSH_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the SSH service task is initialized during system boot, consuming additional RAM for the stack and heap. It requires the TCP/IP stack (e.g., lwIP) to be enabled and configured. If set to 0, the service is excluded from the build, reducing the binary size and freeing up system resources.
EN_SSH_SERVICE.usage: Enable this flag when remote secure shell access is required for debugging, configuration, or file management over Ethernet. Disable it in production environments where security is a concern or when memory constraints are critical. Ensure that the network interface is properly initialized before enabling this service to prevent boot-time crashes.

EN_SSH_TEST.brief: Enables the Secure Shell (SSH) diagnostic interface for remote system debugging.
EN_SSH_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the SSH server task and binds it to the configured network interface. This flag depends on the network stack being enabled (e.g., LWIP_ENABLED). Disabling this (0) saves significant RAM and CPU cycles by removing the SSH daemon and associated encryption buffers.
EN_SSH_TEST.usage: Enable this during the development and integration phase to allow remote access to the system shell for monitoring and troubleshooting. Disable it in production builds to reduce the attack surface and free up memory resources. Ensure that the network stack is fully initialized before this flag is set to 1 to prevent system crashes during boot.

EN_SSH_TRACE.brief: Enables the Secure Shell (SSH) diagnostic tracing mechanism for remote system monitoring.
EN_SSH_TRACE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS routes kernel diagnostic logs to the SSH interface. Disabling this (0) reduces CPU overhead and memory usage. This flag depends on the network stack being initialized and requires the SSH_PORT configuration to be defined.
EN_SSH_TRACE.usage: Enable this during development or field debugging to monitor task states and system health remotely. Disable it in production builds to save flash memory and prevent potential security vulnerabilities associated with exposed diagnostic ports.

EN_STLINK_WAIT_READY.brief: Enables a mandatory delay during system startup to allow the ST-LINK debugger to initialize and attach.
EN_STLINK_WAIT_READY.notes: When set to 1, the system executes a blocking wait loop at the very beginning of main() before the RTOS scheduler starts. If set to 0, the system boots immediately. This flag is independent of other RTOS features but is critical for debugging early-boot code. Typical values are 1 (enabled) for development and 0 (disabled) for production firmware.
EN_STLINK_WAIT_READY.usage: Enable this (1) if you are experiencing hard faults or erratic behavior immediately after power-on or reset while a debugger is connected. It ensures the IDE has time to halt the CPU before the application code runs. Disable this (0) for final production builds to ensure the device starts up instantly without unnecessary delays.

EN_STREAM.brief: Enables the internal stream processing module for asynchronous data handling.
EN_STREAM.notes: When set to 1, the kernel allocates memory for stream buffers and enables stream-related API functions. Disabling this (0) reduces the kernel's static RAM footprint. This flag is a prerequisite for using the caOS communication drivers and must be enabled if any peripheral stream tasks are defined in the project.
EN_STREAM.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires non-blocking data transmission or reception via UART, SPI, or I2C. If your project does not use streaming features, keep it disabled to save memory. Ensure that the heap size is sufficient to accommodate the buffers created when this flag is active.

EN_SW_TIMER.brief: Enables the software timer management module within the caOS kernel.
EN_SW_TIMER.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes the software timer service, allowing tasks to schedule callbacks without hardware timer constraints. Disabling this (0) reduces the kernel's RAM footprint and CPU overhead. This flag must be enabled if any application-level timers or periodic software tasks are utilized.
EN_SW_TIMER.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires non-blocking delays or periodic execution of functions that do not justify a dedicated hardware timer. If you disable this, ensure no part of your code calls timer-related API functions, as this will lead to linker errors or runtime crashes.

EN_SYSLOG_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the internal system logging service for debugging and event tracking.
EN_SYSLOG_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS records system events to a circular buffer or UART output. Disabling it (0) reduces CPU overhead and saves RAM by removing the logging task and buffer allocation. This flag depends on the availability of a configured output peripheral, such as UART or ITM.
EN_SYSLOG_SERVICE.usage: Enable this during the development and integration phase to monitor task switching, error codes, and system health. Disable it in production builds to optimize performance and reduce power consumption. Ensure your logging output peripheral is initialized before the scheduler starts if this is enabled.

EN_TAMP.brief: Enables or disables the hardware tamper detection feature for the system.
EN_TAMP.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes and monitors hardware tamper pins (via ca_exti_tamper_enable). When set to 0, this functionality is disabled, saving memory and CPU cycles. This flag depends on the underlying STM32 hardware support for tamper detection. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_TAMP.usage: Change this value to 1 if your application requires physical security, such as detecting chassis intrusion or unauthorized access to the board. If your hardware design does not include tamper switches or if you do not need this security feature, keep it at 0 to avoid unnecessary interrupt overhead and potential false triggers.

EN_TCP_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the integrated TCP/IP networking stack service within the caOS kernel.
EN_TCP_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the TCP/IP stack and allocates necessary memory buffers for network communication. When set to 0, the stack is excluded from the build, reducing flash and RAM usage. This flag requires the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) for the Ethernet or Wi-Fi peripheral to be correctly configured in the project.
EN_TCP_SERVICE.usage: Set to 1 if your application requires network connectivity (e.g., web server, MQTT, or socket communication). Set to 0 if the device is standalone to save system resources. Warning: Disabling this will cause compilation errors if your application code contains calls to network-related APIs.

EN_TCP_TRACE.brief: Enables or disables the internal diagnostic logging for the TCP/IP stack.
EN_TCP_TRACE.notes: When set to 1, the system outputs detailed packet processing and connection state logs to the debug console. When set to 0, tracing is disabled, reducing CPU overhead and memory usage. This flag depends on the underlying UART or ITM debug interface being initialized.
EN_TCP_TRACE.usage: Set to 1 only during development or when troubleshooting network connectivity issues. Always set to 0 in production builds to prevent performance degradation and excessive log data flooding the serial port.

EN_TFTP_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the built-in Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) server service within the RTOS.
EN_TFTP_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the TFTP stack and binds it to the network interface. This requires the TCP/IP stack (e.g., LwIP) to be enabled and configured. Disabling this (0) reduces the memory footprint and removes the network port dependency.
EN_TFTP_SERVICE.usage: Enable this flag when you need to perform remote firmware updates or configuration file transfers over Ethernet. Ensure that the network stack is fully initialized before this service starts; setting this to 1 without a valid network interface configuration may cause the system to hang during the boot sequence.

EN_TIMER.brief: Enables the internal software timer management system within the caOS kernel.
EN_TIMER.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes the timer task and processes software timer callbacks. If set to 0, all software timer functionality is disabled, reducing RAM and CPU overhead. This flag is a prerequisite for using any os_timer_create or os_timer_start functions. It requires a defined OS_TIMER_TASK_PRIORITY and OS_TIMER_STACK_SIZE in the configuration file.
EN_TIMER.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires periodic tasks or delayed execution events. Disable it if your system is strictly event-driven or resource-constrained to save memory. Warning: Disabling this while application code attempts to start a timer will result in a kernel assertion or undefined behavior.

EN_TLS.brief: Enables or disables the Transport Layer Security (TLS) stack support within the caOS RTOS.
EN_TLS.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the code and memory structures required for TLS communication (e.g., ca_tls_* functions). Disabling this (set to 0) reduces the firmware binary size and RAM usage by excluding cryptographic overhead. This flag is a prerequisite for using secure network services like HTTPS or secure MQTT.
EN_TLS.usage: Enable this flag when your application needs to establish encrypted network connections. If your project does not require secure communication, set this to 0 to save significant flash and heap memory. Ensure that your hardware has sufficient resources, as TLS operations are computationally intensive and require additional memory buffers.

EN_UART_DMA.brief: Enables or disables Direct Memory Access (DMA) support for UART communication peripherals.
EN_UART_DMA.notes: When set to 1, UART data transfers are offloaded to the DMA controller, reducing CPU overhead. When set to 0, the system uses standard interrupt-driven or polling-based I/O. Enabling this requires proper DMA stream/channel configuration in the STM32 CubeMX or hardware abstraction layer. It is typically a boolean flag (0 or 1).
EN_UART_DMA.usage: Set to 1 if your application handles high-speed serial communication or requires low CPU utilization during data transmission. Set to 0 if you are debugging UART issues, have limited DMA resources, or if the application has very low throughput requirements where the overhead of DMA setup is not justified.

EN_UDP_CLIENT.brief: Enables or disables the UDP client functionality within the caOS networking stack.
EN_UDP_CLIENT.notes: When set to 1, the system allocates memory buffers and initializes the UDP socket interface. When set to 0, the UDP client code is excluded from the build, reducing the overall flash memory footprint. This flag depends on the global network stack being enabled in the configuration.
EN_UDP_CLIENT.usage: Set this to 1 only if your application needs to send or receive data via UDP protocols. If your project only uses TCP or does not require network communication, keep this at 0 to save system resources and avoid unnecessary memory allocation.

EN_UDP_SERVER.brief: Enables or disables the built-in UDP server functionality within the caOS network stack.
EN_UDP_SERVER.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the UDP socket listener and allocates memory for the UDP buffer. If set to 0, the UDP server code is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage. This flag depends on the network stack being enabled in the project configuration.
EN_UDP_SERVER.usage: Set to 1 if your application needs to receive or send data via UDP packets. Set to 0 if your device only uses TCP or does not require network communication to save system resources. Ensure that the UDP buffer size is also configured correctly if this flag is enabled.

EN_UPY_AUTOSTART.brief: Enables or disables the automatic startup of the MicroPython interpreter at system boot.
EN_UPY_AUTOSTART.notes: When set to 1, the caOS kernel will automatically initialize the MicroPython environment and attempt to execute a startup script upon system boot. When set to 0 (default), the interpreter remains inactive until manually triggered via the CLI or application code. This flag depends on the presence of the MicroPython module in the build. Typical values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_UPY_AUTOSTART.usage: Change this value to 1 if your application relies on MicroPython scripts for logic or configuration that must run immediately after power-on. Keep it at 0 for production firmware where you want to control the interpreter lifecycle manually using ca_python_start to save memory or prevent unauthorized script execution.

EN_USB.brief: Enables the USB stack and hardware peripheral drivers within the caOS RTOS environment.
EN_USB.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes USB-related memory pools and interrupt handlers. Disabling this (0) reduces the binary footprint and frees up RAM. This flag depends on the hardware abstraction layer (HAL) being configured for USB support in the STM32 CubeMX project.
EN_USB.usage: Set to 1 when your application requires USB communication (e.g., Virtual COM Port, HID, or Mass Storage). Disable it if your project does not use USB to save system resources and avoid potential conflicts with USB interrupt vectors.

EN_USB_CDC.brief: Enables or disables the USB Communications Device Class (CDC) driver stack within the RTOS.
EN_USB_CDC.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the USB peripheral and allocates memory for the CDC buffer and interrupt handlers. When set to 0, the USB stack is completely excluded from the build, reducing flash and RAM usage. This flag depends on the hardware having a USB-capable STM32 peripheral and requires the USB clock configuration to be active in the system clock tree.
EN_USB_CDC.usage: Set to 1 if your application requires a virtual COM port for logging, debugging, or data communication with a PC. Set to 0 if the USB peripheral is not used or if you need to save memory resources. Ensure that if this is enabled, the corresponding USB interrupt priority is correctly configured in the NVIC to avoid blocking the RTOS scheduler.

EN_USB_CUSTOM.brief: Enables or disables the custom USB stack implementation within the caOS RTOS.
EN_USB_CUSTOM.notes: When set to 1, the system uses the custom caOS USB driver; when set to 0, the system defaults to the standard STM32 HAL USB library. This flag requires the USB peripheral clock to be configured in the system clock tree. Disabling this (0) is recommended for standard HID or CDC applications to ensure compatibility with ST-provided drivers.
EN_USB_CUSTOM.usage: Change this to 1 only if you are implementing a proprietary USB class or require low-level control over USB descriptors not supported by the standard HAL. Keep this at 0 for most projects to avoid unnecessary code bloat and potential stability issues with standard USB host controllers.

EN_USB_DBG.brief: Enables or disables the USB-based debug interface for the caOS RTOS.
EN_USB_DBG.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the USB peripheral to stream debug logs and telemetry to a host PC. When set to 0, the USB peripheral is disabled, saving CPU cycles and memory. This flag requires the hardware USB pins to be correctly configured in the board support package (BSP).
EN_USB_DBG.usage: Set to 1 during development to monitor system state and task execution via a serial terminal. Set to 0 for production builds to reduce power consumption and prevent unauthorized access to system logs. Ensure the USB clock is configured in the system clock tree before enabling this flag.

EN_USB_DFU.brief: Enables or disables the USB Device Firmware Upgrade (DFU) bootloader functionality within the RTOS.
EN_USB_DFU.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the USB DFU stack, allowing firmware updates over USB. When set to 0, this feature is disabled, saving flash memory and RAM. This flag requires the USB hardware peripheral to be physically connected and configured in the hardware abstraction layer.
EN_USB_DFU.usage: Set to 1 during the production phase or when field updates are required. Set to 0 during standard development to save resources or if the USB interface is not used. Warning: Disabling this while the device is in the field will prevent remote firmware updates via USB.

EN_USB_FS.brief: Enables the Full-Speed USB peripheral driver within the caOS RTOS stack.
EN_USB_FS.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the USB hardware abstraction layer and allocates memory for USB buffers. This flag depends on the hardware having a physical USB FS controller (e.g., STM32F103 or STM32F407). If set to 0, all USB-related tasks and interrupt service routines are excluded from the build, reducing the binary footprint.
EN_USB_FS.usage: Set this to 1 when your application requires USB communication (CDC, HID, or MSC). You must ensure that the system clock is configured to 48MHz for the USB peripheral to function correctly. Disable this flag if you are not using USB to save RAM and Flash memory, or if you are using a different communication interface like UART or CAN.

EN_USB_HS.brief: Enables or disables the High-Speed (HS) USB peripheral controller driver in the caOS kernel.
EN_USB_HS.notes: When set to 1, the kernel initializes the USB HS hardware abstraction layer and allocates memory for its associated buffers. When set to 0, the peripheral is disabled, saving RAM and flash memory. This flag depends on the hardware having an external ULPI PHY or an integrated HS PHY. Valid values are 0 (disabled) or 1 (enabled).
EN_USB_HS.usage: Set this to 1 only if your specific STM32 board design includes a High-Speed USB PHY and you intend to use USB 2.0 HS communication. If you are using Full-Speed (FS) USB or no USB at all, keep this at 0 to prevent hard faults caused by accessing uninitialized or non-existent hardware registers.

EN_USB_MSC.brief: Enables or disables the USB Mass Storage Class (MSC) driver stack within the RTOS.
EN_USB_MSC.notes: When set to 1, the system initializes the USB peripheral as a storage device (like a flash drive). When set to 0, the USB MSC stack is excluded from the build, reducing flash memory usage and disabling USB storage functionality. This flag depends on the hardware having a USB-capable STM32 peripheral and requires the USB hardware abstraction layer (HAL) to be configured.
EN_USB_MSC.usage: Set this to 1 if your application needs to expose internal memory or an SD card as a drive to a PC. Set to 0 if you are not using USB storage to save code space and avoid unnecessary interrupt overhead. Ensure that the system clock is configured for USB operation (48MHz) before enabling this flag.

EN_USB_NCM.brief: Enables the Network Control Model (NCM) class support for the USB stack.
EN_USB_NCM.notes: When set to 1, the RTOS initializes the USB NCM driver, allowing the device to appear as a virtual Ethernet adapter over USB. This requires the USB peripheral to be configured in Device mode and depends on the underlying USB hardware abstraction layer (HAL) being active. Disabling this (0) removes the NCM stack from the build, reducing flash memory usage. The NCM implementation requires additional RAM for USB buffer management and will increase the overall memory footprint of the application.
EN_USB_NCM.usage: Enable this flag when you need to implement USB-to-Ethernet bridging or RNDIS-like connectivity for network debugging. Change this value only if your application requires USB networking; ensure that the USB clock and GPIO pins are correctly initialized in your board support package before enabling. Warning: Do not enable this flag if your USB peripheral is not properly configured for device mode, as it will cause runtime errors. Typical use cases include firmware update over USB, network monitoring, and remote debugging scenarios.

EN_VNC_SERVICE.brief: Enables or disables the VNC server service within the caOS RTOS.
EN_VNC_SERVICE.notes: When set to 1, the VNC service is compiled into the firmware, allowing remote graphical access to the system. When set to 0, the service is excluded, reducing flash memory usage. This flag is a prerequisite for using ca_vnc_* functions. Enabling this may require additional network stack resources and memory buffers.
EN_VNC_SERVICE.usage: Change this value to 1 only if your application requires remote display or input control via VNC. If your project does not need a graphical interface or remote desktop capabilities, keep it at 0 to save system resources. Ensure your network configuration is sufficient to handle the VNC traffic before enabling.

EN_VNC_TLS.brief: Enables or disables TLS encryption support for the VNC service.
EN_VNC_TLS.notes: When set to 1, the VNC service requires a TLS handshake to establish a secure connection. When set to 0, VNC traffic is transmitted in plaintext. Enabling this flag significantly increases the memory footprint and CPU usage due to cryptographic operations. It requires a properly configured TLS stack and valid certificates.
EN_VNC_TLS.usage: Set to 1 if your application requires secure remote desktop access over untrusted networks. Set to 0 for local debugging or if the system has strict memory constraints and the network is physically isolated. Ensure that the ca_tls_* API is available and initialized before enabling this flag.

EN_WDT.brief: Enables the internal Watchdog Timer (WDT) supervisor for the caOS kernel.
EN_WDT.notes: When set to 1, the kernel periodically resets the hardware watchdog timer. If the system hangs or enters an infinite loop, the WDT will trigger a hardware reset. This flag depends on the hardware-specific WDT peripheral initialization being completed in the board support package. Typical values are 1 (enabled) or 0 (disabled).
EN_WDT.usage: Enable this in production builds to ensure system recovery from unexpected software freezes. Disable it only during debugging sessions when using breakpoints, as the WDT will otherwise trigger a reset while the CPU is halted.

EN_X25519.brief: Enables the X25519 Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) key exchange algorithm within the caOS cryptographic library.
EN_X25519.notes: When set to 1, the system includes the X25519 implementation, increasing the flash memory footprint by approximately 4KB. It requires the hardware random number generator (RNG) peripheral to be initialized. If set to 0, any attempt to call secure handshake functions will result in a compile-time error or a runtime 'feature not supported' exception.
EN_X25519.usage: Enable this flag when your application requires secure key exchange for encrypted communication (e.g., TLS or custom secure protocols). Disable it if you are strictly optimizing for code space and your project does not perform asymmetric key exchanges. Ensure your STM32 chip has sufficient flash capacity before enabling.

EN_X25519_TEST.brief: Enables the built-in self-test suite for the X25519 elliptic curve cryptography module.
EN_X25519_TEST.notes: When set to 1, the system executes a series of known-answer tests (KAT) during the kernel initialization phase. If set to 0, these tests are skipped, reducing boot time and flash memory footprint. This flag depends on the presence of the cryptographic library module in the build configuration.
EN_X25519_TEST.usage: Enable this flag during the development and integration phase to verify that the X25519 implementation is functioning correctly on the target STM32 hardware. It is recommended to disable this (set to 0) in production firmware to minimize startup latency and prevent potential security side-channel exposure during the test execution.

ETH_MPU_REGION.brief: Defines the Memory Protection Unit (MPU) region index reserved for the Ethernet DMA descriptor memory space.
ETH_MPU_REGION.notes: This constant assigns a specific MPU slot (0-7) to the Ethernet peripheral's memory buffers. Enabling this ensures the MPU correctly marks the Ethernet memory as non-cacheable or shareable to prevent data coherency issues. It is strictly dependent on the hardware architecture; all supported STM32 variants currently require index 5. Changing this value without updating the corresponding MPU configuration table will lead to memory access faults or Ethernet driver failure.
ETH_MPU_REGION.usage: This value should generally remain at 5U for all supported STM32 targets. You should only modify this if you are porting caOS to a new MCU architecture where region 5 is already occupied by another critical system peripheral or if the hardware memory map requires a different slot allocation to avoid overlapping protection regions.

ETH_P_ARP.brief: The Ethernet protocol identifier for the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP).
ETH_P_ARP.notes: This constant represents the EtherType field value (0x0806) used in Ethernet frames to indicate that the payload contains an ARP packet. It is a fixed standard defined by IEEE 802.3. Changing this value will cause the network stack to ignore all incoming ARP requests and replies, effectively breaking IPv4 address resolution.
ETH_P_ARP.usage: This value should never be changed in standard network applications. It is used by the caOS network driver to filter incoming Ethernet frames and identify which packets should be passed to the ARP handler. If you are debugging raw Ethernet frames and notice that ARP packets are not being processed, verify that the hardware filter or the driver's receive logic is correctly comparing the incoming EtherType against this constant.

ETH_P_IP.brief: The Ethernet protocol identifier for the Internet Protocol (IPv4) packet type.
ETH_P_IP.notes: This constant represents the EtherType field value 0x0800, which signals that the payload of an Ethernet frame is an IPv4 packet. It is a standard value defined by IEEE 802.3. Changing this value will cause the network stack to ignore all incoming IPv4 traffic, as the hardware or driver will fail to match the frame type.
ETH_P_IP.usage: This value should generally remain unchanged as it is a fixed networking standard. You would only reference this constant when writing custom packet filters, raw socket handlers, or low-level Ethernet driver logic to identify or construct IPv4 frames. Do not modify this value unless you are implementing a non-standard protocol stack.

ETH_P_IPV6.brief: Defines the Ethernet protocol identifier for IPv6 packets.
ETH_P_IPV6.notes: This constant represents the EtherType value 0x86DD used in the Ethernet frame header to indicate that the payload is an IPv6 packet. It is a fixed standard defined by IEEE 802.3. Changing this value will cause the network stack to fail to recognize or process any incoming IPv6 traffic, as the hardware/driver will no longer match the frame type correctly.
ETH_P_IPV6.usage: This value should generally never be changed as it is defined by international networking standards. You would only reference this constant when writing custom packet filters, raw socket handlers, or debugging the network stack to verify that the Ethernet layer is correctly identifying IPv6 frames.

ETH_P_VLAN.brief: Defines the standard IEEE 802.1Q EtherType value used to identify VLAN-tagged Ethernet frames.
ETH_P_VLAN.notes: This constant represents the hex value 0x8100, which is the global standard for VLAN tagging. When enabled in the network stack, the system will parse incoming frames for this specific header to extract VLAN IDs. It is a read-only configuration for the protocol parser and should not be modified unless working with non-standard or proprietary network encapsulation.
ETH_P_VLAN.usage: Use this value when configuring the Ethernet MAC filter or the packet inspection layer to ensure the RTOS correctly identifies and strips VLAN tags. Do not change this value for standard network communication, as doing so will cause the stack to ignore all standard VLAN-tagged traffic.

FAT_CRYPT_CHUNK.brief: Defines the size in bytes of the data buffer used for cryptographic operations within the FAT file system driver.
FAT_CRYPT_CHUNK.notes: This constant determines the memory footprint of the encryption/decryption buffer. It must be a multiple of the underlying storage sector size (typically 512 bytes). Increasing this value can improve throughput for large file operations but will consume more RAM from the heap or static pool. It is strictly dependent on the hardware's DMA alignment requirements.
FAT_CRYPT_CHUNK.usage: Adjust this value if you encounter performance bottlenecks during file I/O or if you need to optimize RAM usage on memory-constrained STM32 devices. Ensure the value is a power of two to maintain compatibility with standard FAT sector alignment. Setting this too low may increase CPU overhead due to frequent context switching during encryption tasks.

FB_COPY_MS.brief: Defines the timeout in milliseconds for frame buffer copy operations.
FB_COPY_MS.notes: This constant controls the maximum time the system waits for a frame buffer copy (e.g., using ca_dma2d_copy) to complete before timing out. It is typically used in display drivers or graphics tasks. If the value is too low, complex screen updates may fail; if too high, it may block the calling task for an excessive duration during hardware contention.
FB_COPY_MS.usage: Increase this value if you observe intermittent graphical glitches or timeout errors during heavy screen updates. Decrease it only if you need to ensure the system remains responsive under high load and you are certain the hardware can complete the copy within the shorter window.

FFCONF_DEF.brief: Defines the character encoding or code page used by the FatFs file system layer.
FFCONF_DEF.notes: This constant determines how FatFs handles character sets for file names. The value 80386 is a specific identifier for the OEM code page (typically CP850 or similar depending on the FatFs implementation). Changing this affects how non-ASCII characters are interpreted in file names. It is a static configuration value defined in the FatFs header.
FFCONF_DEF.usage: Change this value only if you need to support specific regional character sets (e.g., switching between different OEM code pages) for file system compatibility. Incorrect values may result in file names appearing corrupted or being inaccessible when using non-standard characters. Ensure the chosen code page is supported by the underlying FatFs library configuration.

FF_CODE_PAGE.brief: Defines the character encoding (code page) used by the FAT file system for file names.
FF_CODE_PAGE.notes: This constant determines how non-ASCII characters in file names are interpreted. Setting this to 850 enables support for the Latin-1 (Western European) character set. Changing this value affects how the file system driver maps bytes to characters; it does not require additional dependencies but must be consistent with the files stored on the media to avoid corrupted file name displays.
FF_CODE_PAGE.usage: Change this value if your application needs to support specific regional characters (e.g., accented letters) in file names. If you only use standard English alphanumeric characters, the default is sufficient. Ensure the value matches the encoding used by the host system that created the files, otherwise, file names may appear with incorrect symbols when using ca_fat_ls.

FF_FS_CRTIME.brief: Enables or disables support for file creation time tracking in the FAT filesystem.
FF_FS_CRTIME.notes: When set to 1, the filesystem stores the creation timestamp for files and directories. When set to 0 (default), this feature is disabled, saving a small amount of metadata space per file entry. This flag is independent of the modification time tracking. Enabling this requires the underlying hardware or RTC to provide accurate time data via ca_rtc_get.
FF_FS_CRTIME.usage: Change this to 1 if your application requires auditing or logging of when specific files were generated. Keep it at 0 for standard embedded storage tasks where only modification time is relevant, as it reduces the overhead on the FAT table entries.

FF_FS_EXFAT.brief: Enables or disables support for the exFAT file system format in FatFs.
FF_FS_EXFAT.notes: When set to 1, the system includes code to handle exFAT volumes, which increases the memory footprint of the FatFs library. When set to 0 (default), exFAT support is disabled, saving flash and RAM. This flag is independent of FAT12/FAT16/FAT32 support. Enabling this requires additional stack space for complex file system operations.
FF_FS_EXFAT.usage: Change this to 1 only if your application specifically requires reading or writing to SD cards or storage media formatted with the exFAT file system. If you only use standard FAT32, keep this at 0 to conserve system resources. Warning: Enabling this on memory-constrained STM32 devices may lead to stack overflow or flash exhaustion.

FF_FS_LOCK.brief: Configures the file locking mechanism for the FAT filesystem to prevent concurrent access conflicts.
FF_FS_LOCK.notes: When set to 0, file locking is disabled. If set to a value > 0, it enables file locking, where the value represents the maximum number of open files that can be tracked for locking. Enabling this requires additional memory for the lock table. This flag is independent of other caOS RTOS primitives but affects the behavior of ca_fat_fopen and ca_fat_fclose.
FF_FS_LOCK.usage: Keep this at 0 for simple, single-threaded applications to save memory. Increase this value only if your application performs concurrent file operations from multiple tasks and you need to prevent data corruption or race conditions during file access. Do not set this to a high value if your system has limited RAM, as it allocates a static table.

FF_FS_MINIMIZE.brief: Controls the level of FatFS API features enabled to save code space.
FF_FS_MINIMIZE.notes: When set to 0, all FatFS features are enabled (full API). Values 1, 2, or 3 progressively disable specific functions (like f_rename, f_mkdir, f_chmod, etc.) to reduce the binary footprint. This flag is a standard FatFS configuration option; setting it to 0 is the default for full functionality.
FF_FS_MINIMIZE.usage: Change this value only if your application is running out of Flash memory and you do not require advanced file system operations. If you need to rename files or create directories, keep this at 0. If you only need basic read/write access, you may increase this value to 1 or 2 to save space, but be aware that functions like ca_fat_prename or ca_fat_mkdir will become unavailable.

FF_FS_NOFSINFO.brief: Disables the FSINFO sector support in FATFS to save memory and reduce disk access.
FF_FS_NOFSINFO.notes: When set to 0 (enabled), FATFS uses the FSINFO sector to track free clusters and the last allocated cluster, speeding up file creation. When set to 1 (disabled), FATFS ignores this sector, which saves a small amount of RAM but forces the system to scan the FAT table to find free space, significantly slowing down write operations on large volumes. This flag is typically used on small embedded systems where RAM is extremely limited or the storage media does not support FSINFO.
FF_FS_NOFSINFO.usage: Set this to 1 only if you are experiencing memory exhaustion or if your specific storage media (e.g., certain older SD cards or custom flash partitions) does not correctly implement the FSINFO sector. For most standard applications, keep this at 0 to ensure optimal performance during file system write operations.

FF_FS_NORTC.brief: Disables the Real-Time Clock (RTC) dependency for file timestamps in the FAT filesystem.
FF_FS_NORTC.notes: When set to 1, the filesystem ignores the system RTC for file modification times. This reduces code size and removes the requirement for a hardware RTC or time-keeping service. If set to 0, the system expects a valid time source to be available via ca_rtc_get to timestamp files correctly.
FF_FS_NORTC.usage: Set this to 1 if your application does not require accurate file creation or modification dates, or if the hardware lacks a battery-backed RTC. This is common in simple data logging applications where only the file content matters. If you need to track when files were created, set this to 0 and ensure ca_rtc_init is called during system startup.

FF_FS_REENTRANT.brief: Enables or disables reentrancy support for the FatFs file system.
FF_FS_REENTRANT.notes: When set to 0, FatFs is not thread-safe, meaning only one task can access the file system at a time. When set to 1, it enables reentrancy, requiring an OS-dependent synchronization object (mutex) to be provided via the 'ff_req_grant' and 'ff_rel_grant' functions. Enabling this increases memory usage and requires the implementation of OS-specific locking mechanisms.
FF_FS_REENTRANT.usage: Keep this at 0 if your application is single-threaded or if you manually ensure that only one task performs file operations at any given time. Change this to 1 only if multiple tasks need to access the file system concurrently, in which case you must implement the necessary mutex logic to prevent data corruption.

FF_FS_TINY.brief: Enables the 'Tiny' configuration mode for the FatFS file system to minimize memory footprint.
FF_FS_TINY.notes: When set to 1, FatFS operates in a reduced-feature mode, disabling support for long file names (LFN), multiple volumes, and advanced features like f_mkfs or f_rename. This significantly reduces RAM and Flash usage. When set to 0 (default), full FatFS features are enabled. This flag is a compile-time configuration and requires a full project rebuild if changed.
FF_FS_TINY.usage: Change this to 1 only if your STM32 device has extremely limited RAM/Flash and you only need basic file read/write operations (8.3 format filenames). Do not enable this if your application requires long file names, directory manipulation, or complex file system management, as those functions will be removed from the API.

FF_LBA64.brief: Enables or disables 64-bit Logical Block Addressing (LBA) support for FATFS.
FF_LBA64.notes: When set to 1, FATFS supports disks larger than 2TB (using 64-bit addressing). When set to 0 (default), it is limited to 32-bit LBA, supporting disks up to 2TB. Enabling this increases the memory footprint of the FATFS layer slightly and requires the underlying storage driver to support 64-bit sector addressing.
FF_LBA64.usage: Change this to 1 only if your application must interface with storage media larger than 2TB. For most embedded STM32 applications using SD cards or internal flash, 0 is sufficient and preferred to save resources. Ensure your hardware abstraction layer (e.g., ca_sdio or ca_qspi) is capable of handling 64-bit sector offsets before enabling.

FF_LFN_BUF.brief: Defines the maximum buffer size in bytes for Long File Names (LFN) in the FAT filesystem.
FF_LFN_BUF.notes: This constant allocates memory for the LFN buffer. Increasing this value allows for longer file names but consumes more RAM. The value 255 is the maximum allowed by the FAT specification for a single path component. It is typically used in conjunction with other FAT configuration flags to manage memory footprint on resource-constrained STM32 devices.
FF_LFN_BUF.usage: Change this value if you need to support very long file names and have sufficient RAM available. If you encounter errors when accessing files with long names, ensure this buffer is large enough. Warning: setting this value too high on a device with limited RAM may lead to stack overflow or heap exhaustion; always verify memory usage using ca_top or ca_memory_info.

FF_LFN_UNICODE.brief: Configures whether the FAT filesystem supports Unicode characters in long file names.
FF_LFN_UNICODE.notes: When set to 0, the system uses standard ASCII/ANSI encoding for file names. Setting this to 1, 2, or 3 enables Unicode support (UTF-16 or UTF-8), which increases the memory footprint of the FAT driver and requires additional code space. This flag is typically disabled (0) in resource-constrained embedded systems to save RAM and Flash.
FF_LFN_UNICODE.usage: Change this value to 1 or higher only if your application must handle file names containing non-ASCII characters (e.g., international symbols). If you only use standard alphanumeric characters, keep it at 0 to minimize the memory overhead of the ca_fat_* API operations.

FF_MAX_LFN.brief: Defines the maximum length of Long File Names (LFN) supported by the FAT filesystem in bytes.
FF_MAX_LFN.notes: This constant determines the buffer size allocated for handling long filenames. Valid values range from 12 to 255. Increasing this value consumes more stack or heap memory during file operations. It is a dependency for enabling LFN support in the FAT configuration.
FF_MAX_LFN.usage: Change this value if you need to support longer filenames than the default (e.g., for complex directory structures or specific file naming conventions). If you encounter errors when opening files with long names, ensure this value is sufficient. Warning: setting this too high may lead to stack overflow in tasks that perform file operations.

FF_MAX_SS.brief: Defines the maximum sector size in bytes supported by the FAT file system.
FF_MAX_SS.notes: This constant sets the upper limit for the sector size buffer used by the FATFS layer. The value 512 is the standard for most SD cards and flash storage. If your hardware or storage media requires 4096-byte sectors (Advanced Format), this value must be updated accordingly. Increasing this value consumes more RAM in the FATFS work buffer.
FF_MAX_SS.usage: Change this value only if you are interfacing with storage media that uses non-standard sector sizes (e.g., 4096 bytes). Using an incorrect value will result in mount failures or data corruption when calling ca_fat_mount or performing file I/O operations.

FF_MIN_GPT.brief: Defines the minimum granularity for FATFS cluster allocation or internal buffer alignment.
FF_MIN_GPT.notes: This constant sets a threshold for memory management within the FATFS layer. Enabling or adjusting this value affects how the file system handles cluster allocation and buffer alignment. It is typically used to ensure that memory operations align with the underlying hardware's DMA requirements or flash sector boundaries. Valid values are typically powers of two, with 0x10000000 being a specific architectural alignment constant for the caOS FATFS implementation.
