ca_mqtt_disconnected_cb_t.usage: Use this to implement reconnection logic, update UI status indicators, or trigger system-wide alerts when the MQTT connection drops.

ca_mqtt_message_cb_t.brief: A callback function pointer type used to handle incoming MQTT messages received by the caOS MQTT client.

members.name: topic
members.desc: Pointer to the string containing the MQTT topic. Note: this string is not guaranteed to be null-terminated.

members.name: topic_len
members.desc: The length of the topic string. Always use this value to process the topic safely.

members.name: payload
members.desc: Pointer to the raw data buffer received in the MQTT message.

members.name: payload_len
members.desc: The size of the payload in bytes.

ca_mqtt_message_cb_t.notes: The callback is executed within the context of the MQTT service task. Keep the implementation short and non-blocking to avoid delaying other network operations. The memory pointed to by topic and payload is managed by the MQTT stack and is only valid for the duration of the callback execution.
ca_mqtt_message_cb_t.usage: Used when subscribing to MQTT topics. You pass a function pointer of this type to the subscription API to define the logic that executes whenever a message arrives on a specific topic.
ca_mqtt_message_cb_t.example: void my_mqtt_handler(const char *topic, u16 topic_len, const uint8_t *payload, u16 payload_len) { if (payload_len > 0) { printf("Received message on topic: %.*s\n", topic_len, topic); } } // Usage: ca_mqtt_subscribe(client, "sensors/temp", my_mqtt_handler);

ca_mutex_t.brief: A mutual exclusion primitive used to protect shared resources from concurrent access by multiple tasks.

members.name: owner
members.desc: Stores the handle of the task currently holding the mutex. Do not modify manually.

members.name: locked
members.desc: Status flag: 0 means the mutex is available, 1 means it is currently held by a task.

members.name: wait_queue
members.desc: Internal list of tasks blocked while waiting for this mutex to become available.

members.name: internal_lock
members.desc: A low-level spinlock used to ensure atomic operations on the mutex structure itself.

members.name: pi_next
members.desc: Pointer used for Priority Inheritance (PI) tracking to link multiple mutexes held by the same task.

ca_mutex_t.notes: The mutex must be initialized before use. It is typically allocated in the global data segment or as part of a larger control block. Ownership is managed by the RTOS kernel; never attempt to manually set the 'owner' or 'locked' fields, as this will corrupt the scheduler's synchronization logic.
ca_mutex_t.usage: Use this type to prevent race conditions when multiple tasks access the same peripheral or global variable. It is passed to synchronization APIs to lock and unlock critical sections.

ca_net_buf_meta_t.brief: A union structure representing the metadata associated with a network buffer, used to store either RX or TX specific protocol information.

members.name: rx
members.desc: Metadata structure for incoming packets. Contains fields like protocol type, source/destination ports, and checksum status. Only valid when the buffer is in RX mode.

members.name: tx
members.desc: Metadata structure for outgoing packets. Contains fields like destination address and transmission flags. Only valid when the buffer is in TX mode.

members.name: raw
members.desc: A raw byte array of 52 bytes used to access the memory directly or to ensure the union size is fixed for memory alignment and buffer pool management.

ca_net_buf_meta_t.notes: This union is part of the ca_net_buf_t structure. It does not require manual allocation as it is embedded within the buffer object. The developer must ensure they only access the member corresponding to the current direction of the packet (RX or TX) to avoid data corruption.
ca_net_buf_meta_t.usage: Used by the network stack to track packet state as it moves through the OSI layers. You will typically access this when writing custom protocol handlers or inspecting packet headers in a callback.

ca_net_buf_pressure_t.brief: A structure used to monitor the health and memory usage of the network buffer pool.

members.name: total
members.desc: The total number of network buffers available in the system pool.

members.name: free_now
members.desc: The number of buffers currently available for allocation.

members.name: free_min
members.desc: The lowest number of free buffers recorded since the last system reset; useful for detecting memory pressure spikes.

members.name: alloc_calls
members.desc: Total number of allocation requests made to the pool since the last reset.

members.name: alloc_fail
members.desc: Number of allocation requests that failed because the pool was empty.

ca_net_buf_pressure_t.notes: This structure is populated by the system. It does not require manual allocation or initialization by the user. It is typically used to diagnose network stability issues or to tune the buffer pool size.
ca_net_buf_pressure_t.usage: Use this structure with ca_net_buf_pressure to retrieve current statistics. If the alloc_fail count is increasing, your system is running out of network buffers, which may lead to dropped packets or connection failures.

ca_net_buf_rx_t.body:
typedef struct {
u16    l3_off;   /* frame offset to L3 header: 14 no-VLAN, 18 with 802.1Q */
u16    l4_off;   /* frame offset to L4 header: l3_off + IP IHL; 0 if none */
ca_ipv4_t src_ip;   /* IPv4 src (spa for ARP, 0 if non-IP)                   */
ca_ipv4_t dst_ip;   /* IPv4 dst (tpa for ARP, 0 if non-IP)                   */
u16    src_port; /* UDP/TCP source port (0 if non UDP/TCP)                */
u16    dst_port; /* UDP/TCP dest   port (0 if non UDP/TCP)                */
u16    vlan_id;  /* 802.1Q VID (0 = untagged)                             */
u8     vlan_pcp; /* 802.1Q PCP (0-7)                                      */
u8     ip_proto; /* IP_PROTO_ICMP=1 / UDP=17 / TCP=6; 0 if non-IP        */
u8     iface;    /* ingress iface id (ca_net_iface_t.id): replies go back
out of it                                            */
} ca_net_buf_rx_t;                                               /* 24 bytes */
ca_net_buf_rx_t.brief: A metadata structure containing parsed network header offsets and addresses for an incoming packet buffer.

members.name: l3_off
members.desc: Byte offset from the start of the buffer to the Layer 3 (IP/ARP) header. Typically 14 for Ethernet II or 18 if 802.1Q VLAN tagged.

members.name: l4_off
members.desc: Byte offset to the Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) header. Set to 0 if the packet is not a transport layer protocol.

members.name: src_ip
members.desc: Source IPv4 address extracted from the packet header. Set to 0 for non-IP packets.

members.name: dst_ip
members.desc: Destination IPv4 address extracted from the packet header. Set to 0 for non-IP packets.

members.name: src_port
members.desc: Source port for TCP/UDP packets. Set to 0 if the protocol is not TCP or UDP.

members.name: dst_port
members.desc: Destination port for TCP/UDP packets. Set to 0 if the protocol is not TCP or UDP.

members.name: vlan_id
members.desc: The 802.1Q VLAN ID (VID). Value 0 indicates the packet is untagged.

members.name: vlan_pcp
members.desc: The 802.1Q Priority Code Point (PCP). Valid range is 0-7.

members.name: ip_proto
members.desc: The IP protocol number (e.g., 1 for ICMP, 6 for TCP, 17 for UDP). Set to 0 if not an IP packet.

ca_net_buf_rx_t.notes: This structure is typically populated by the caOS network stack driver during packet reception. It is read-only for the application layer. Do not manually modify these fields as they are used by the stack to route packets to the correct socket or handler.
ca_net_buf_rx_t.usage: Used by network callback functions or packet processing tasks to inspect packet headers without manually parsing raw bytes. It allows for efficient filtering of incoming traffic based on IP or port.

ca_net_buf_t.brief: A network buffer structure used to store packet data and metadata during transmission or reception in the caOS network stack.

members.name: next
members.desc: Index of the next buffer in a chain. Use NET_BUF_INVALID if this is the last buffer.

members.name: data_off
members.desc: Offset in bytes from the start of the data array to the actual payload. Must be within [0, NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE].

members.name: data_len
members.desc: Length of the payload in bytes. Must not exceed the remaining space in the data array.

members.name: flags
members.desc: Bitmask of NET_BUF_F_* flags indicating buffer state or packet properties.

members.name: proto
members.desc: Protocol identifier (NET_PROTO_*) assigned by the L2 dispatcher.

members.name: timestamp
members.desc: System tick value captured at the moment of frame reception.

members.name: meta
members.desc: Internal cache for L2/L3/L4 parsing results and routing information.

members.name: data
members.desc: The raw memory buffer where packet data is stored.

ca_net_buf_t.notes: Buffers are typically managed by the caOS network pool. Do not manually allocate these on the stack as they are large (2KB). Ownership is transferred to the network stack once passed to transmission functions.
ca_net_buf_t.usage: Used by network drivers and protocol layers to pass packet data through the stack. Always initialize the buffer via the network pool API before use.

ca_net_buf_tx_t.brief: A structure defining the network layer routing information required to transmit a UDP packet.

members.name: dst_ip
members.desc: The target IPv4 address. Must be a valid unicast or broadcast address.

members.name: dst_port
members.desc: The destination UDP port number. Values 0-65535 are valid.

members.name: src_port
members.desc: The source UDP port number. Usually assigned by the application.

members.name: dst_mac
members.desc: The resolved hardware MAC address of the destination. Must be populated via ARP resolution before transmission.

ca_net_buf_tx_t.notes: This structure is typically allocated on the stack by the application layer. It does not own any memory buffers; it acts as a header descriptor for the network stack to encapsulate data into an Ethernet frame. Ensure the dst_mac is correctly resolved via the ARP table before passing this struct to the transmission API.
ca_net_buf_tx_t.usage: Used as a parameter in network transmission functions to specify the routing metadata for outgoing UDP datagrams.

ca_net_cfg_t.brief: Configuration structure used to initialize the caOS network stack with hardware and protocol settings.

members.name: ip
members.desc: The static IPv4 address for the device. If using DHCP, this may be ignored or overwritten.

members.name: mask
members.desc: The subnet mask. Set to 0 if the network configuration is handled dynamically via DHCP.

members.name: mac
members.desc: The unique 6-byte hardware MAC address for the Ethernet interface.

members.name: mtu
members.desc: Maximum Transmission Unit. Set to 0 to use the default value of 1500 bytes.

members.name: phy_nrst_port
members.desc: GPIO port index for the PHY reset pin. Use 0xFF if the PHY reset is not connected to a GPIO.

members.name: phy_nrst_pin
members.desc: GPIO pin number (0-15) for the PHY reset. Only relevant if phy_nrst_port is not 0xFF.

members.name: arp
members.desc: Configuration parameters for the ARP protocol layer.

members.name: udp
members.desc: Configuration parameters for the UDP protocol layer.

members.name: icmp
members.desc: Configuration parameters for the ICMP (ping) protocol layer.

ca_net_cfg_t.notes: This structure must be populated before calling the network initialization function. It is typically declared as a static constant or global variable to ensure it persists throughout the application lifecycle. Fields dependent on preprocessor macros (like DHCP or MQTT) are only available if those features are enabled in the project configuration.
ca_net_cfg_t.usage: Use this struct to define the network identity and protocol behavior of your device. Pass a pointer to this structure to the network stack initialization function during system startup.

ca_net_filter_fn_t.brief: A callback function type used to inspect or modify network packets before they are processed by the stack.

members.name: buf_idx
members.desc: The index of the network buffer in the internal pool. Valid range is 0 to (MAX_NET_BUFFERS - 1). Passing an invalid index will cause an out-of-bounds access.

ca_net_filter_fn_t.notes: This callback is executed within the context of the network task. It must be kept short and non-blocking to avoid dropping incoming packets. The user does not allocate the buffer; they only receive the index to perform operations via the net_buf_get/set APIs.
ca_net_filter_fn_t.usage: Used to implement custom packet filtering, firewalling, or packet inspection. It is registered with the network stack during initialization to intercept incoming traffic.

ca_net_handler_t.brief: A callback function pointer type used by the network stack to process incoming network buffers.

members.name: buf_idx
members.desc: The index of the network buffer in the internal pool. Use this index with ca_net_buf_ptr to access the data.

ca_net_handler_t.notes: This callback is typically invoked by the network stack when a packet is received. The handler is responsible for processing the data and must eventually call ca_net_buf_free to release the buffer back to the pool. Failure to free the buffer will lead to a memory leak in the network buffer pool.
ca_net_handler_t.usage: Used when registering custom protocol handlers or packet processors via ca_net_register. It allows the application to intercept specific network traffic.

ca_net_mac_filter_fn_t.brief: A callback function type used to filter incoming network packets based on their MAC address or interface.

members.name: buf_idx
members.desc: The index of the network buffer containing the packet to be inspected.

members.name: iface
members.desc: The interface identifier where the packet was received.

ca_net_mac_filter_fn_t.notes: The callback must return true to accept the packet or false to drop it. It is typically registered via ca_net_filter_set. Ensure the logic inside is fast, as it runs within the network processing context.
ca_net_mac_filter_fn_t.usage: Use this to implement custom firewall rules or packet filtering logic at the link layer. Register the function using ca_net_filter_set to enable the filtering mechanism.

ca_net_queue_t.brief: A circular buffer structure used for thread-safe communication of network packets between an ISR and the network task.

members.name: buf
members.desc: The underlying storage array for packet descriptors or indices. Must be sized to NET_QUEUE_DEPTH.

members.name: head
members.desc: The read index. Only the consumer (network task) should modify this value.

members.name: tail
members.desc: The write index. Only the producer (ISR) should modify this value.

ca_net_queue_t.notes: This structure implements a lock-free single-producer single-consumer (SPSC) queue. It relies on the volatile keyword to prevent compiler optimization of index access. The user is responsible for ensuring that the queue is not overflowed by the producer, as there is no built-in bounds checking in the struct itself.
ca_net_queue_t.usage: Use this type when you need to pass data from a hardware interrupt (e.g., Ethernet RX interrupt) to a background processing task without using heavy synchronization primitives like mutexes.

ca_net_stats_t.body:
typedef struct {
u32 rx_frames;        /* frames received */
u32 rx_dropped_pool;  /* dropped: pool exhausted */
u32 rx_dropped_small; /* dropped: frame < 14 bytes */
u32 rx_no_handler;    /* received but no handler registered */
u32 tx_frames;        /* frames sent */
u32 tx_failed;        /* iface->send() returned false */
u32 err_bus;          /* CA_ETH_ERR_BUS events */
u32 err_rbu;          /* CA_ETH_ERR_RBU events */
u32 process_calls;    /* how many times ca_net_process() was called */
u32 rx_dropped_vlan;  /* dropped: 802.1Q tag with a VLAN id (only the
priority tag, VID 0, is taken - and stripped) */
} ca_net_stats_t;
ca_net_stats_t.brief: A structure containing diagnostic counters for the network stack, used to monitor traffic and identify packet loss or hardware errors.

members.name: rx_frames
members.desc: Total number of Ethernet frames successfully received.

members.name: rx_dropped_pool
members.desc: Frames dropped because the network buffer pool was exhausted.

members.name: rx_dropped_small
members.desc: Frames dropped because they were smaller than the minimum required size (14 bytes).

members.name: rx_no_handler
members.desc: Frames received for which no protocol handler was registered.

members.name: tx_frames
members.desc: Total number of Ethernet frames successfully sent.

members.name: tx_failed
members.desc: Frames that failed to send because the interface driver returned an error.

members.name: err_bus
members.desc: Count of CA_ETH_ERR_BUS hardware events.

members.name: err_rbu
members.desc: Count of CA_ETH_ERR_RBU hardware events.

members.name: process_calls
members.desc: Number of times the network processing loop was executed.

ca_net_stats_t.notes: The structure is populated by the network stack. The user is responsible for providing a valid pointer to a ca_net_stats_t variable to the ca_net_stats() function, which will fill it with current values. It does not require manual allocation if declared on the stack.
ca_net_stats_t.usage: Use this type to perform periodic health checks on the network interface. It is typically called within a monitoring task to log network performance or detect connectivity issues.

ca_ntp_cfg_t.brief: Configuration structure used to define the parameters for the NTP (Network Time Protocol) client service.

members.name: server_ip
members.desc: The IPv4 address of the NTP server to synchronize with. Must be a valid network-byte-order address.

members.name: poll_ms
members.desc: The interval in milliseconds between synchronization attempts. If set to 0, the system defaults to 64000ms.

members.name: on_synced
members.desc: A callback function pointer triggered whenever the system time is successfully updated. Can be set to NULL if no notification is required.

ca_ntp_cfg_t.notes: The structure is typically passed by value or pointer to the NTP initialization function. The user is responsible for allocating this struct, usually in static memory or on the stack before starting the network stack. Ensure the server_ip is reachable via the current network configuration.
ca_ntp_cfg_t.usage: Use this structure when configuring the caOS network stack to enable automatic time synchronization. It is passed to the NTP client initialization routine to define the server target and the frequency of updates.

ca_ntp_fail_cb_t.brief: A callback function type triggered by the NTP service when a time synchronization attempt fails.

members.name: void
members.desc: The callback takes no arguments and returns no value.

ca_ntp_fail_cb_t.notes: This callback is executed within the context of the NTP service task. It must be kept short and non-blocking to avoid delaying network synchronization tasks. It is typically registered during the initialization of the NTP service.
ca_ntp_fail_cb_t.usage: Use this to implement custom error handling or logging when the device fails to reach an NTP server, such as triggering a system status LED or attempting a network interface reset.

ca_ntp_pkt_t.brief: Represents a standard NTP (Network Time Protocol) packet structure used for network time synchronization.

members.name: li_vn_mode
members.desc: Bitfield containing Leap Indicator (2 bits), Version Number (3 bits), and Mode (3 bits).

members.name: stratum
members.desc: Indicates the distance from the reference clock (0 = unspecified, 1 = primary reference).

members.name: poll
members.desc: Maximum interval between successive messages, in log2 seconds.

members.name: precision
members.desc: Precision of the local clock, in log2 seconds.

members.name: root_delay
members.desc: Total round-trip delay to the reference clock, in 16.16 fixed-point format.

members.name: root_dispersion
members.desc: Maximum error relative to the reference clock, in 16.16 fixed-point format.

members.name: ref_id
members.desc: Reference clock identifier.

members.name: ref_ts_s
members.desc: Reference timestamp seconds part.

members.name: ref_ts_f
members.desc: Reference timestamp fraction part.

members.name: org_ts_s
members.desc: Origin timestamp seconds part (client transmit time).

members.name: org_ts_f
members.desc: Origin timestamp fraction part.

members.name: rec_ts_s
members.desc: Receive timestamp seconds part (server receive time).

members.name: rec_ts_f
members.desc: Receive timestamp fraction part.

members.name: xmt_ts_s
members.desc: Transmit timestamp seconds part (server transmit time).

members.name: xmt_ts_f
members.desc: Transmit timestamp fraction part.

ca_ntp_pkt_t.notes: The struct is marked with __attribute__((packed)) to ensure no padding bytes are inserted by the compiler, which is critical for network protocol compliance. All multi-byte fields are typically expected in Network Byte Order (Big Endian).
ca_ntp_pkt_t.usage: Used when constructing NTP request packets to be sent to a time server or when parsing the response packet received from a server to calculate network latency and clock offset.

ca_ntp_sync_cb_t.brief: A callback function type triggered by the NTP service when a time synchronization event completes.

members.name: unix_time
members.desc: The current time in seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1, 1970). If the value is 0, it indicates a synchronization failure.

ca_ntp_sync_cb_t.notes: This callback is executed within the context of the NTP service task. It must be kept short and non-blocking to avoid delaying network stack operations. The user does not allocate this; it is registered via the NTP service configuration.
ca_ntp_sync_cb_t.usage: Use this callback to update the system RTC or application-level timestamps immediately after the device successfully synchronizes with an NTP server.

ca_ntp_synced_t.body: typedef void (*ca_ntp_synced_t)(u32 unix_time);  /* called on sync */
ca_ntp_synced_t.brief: A callback function pointer triggered by the caOS network stack when an NTP time synchronization event completes successfully.

members.name: unix_time
members.desc: The current time in seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1, 1970). This value is provided by the NTP server and represents the synchronized system time.

ca_ntp_synced_t.notes: This callback is executed within the context of the network task. It must be kept short and non-blocking to avoid delaying network packet processing. The user is responsible for assigning a valid function pointer to this type in the network configuration structure before the network stack is initialized.
ca_ntp_synced_t.usage: Used during the initialization of the caOS network stack. It allows the application to be notified immediately when the system clock has been updated via NTP, which is useful for logging, scheduling, or updating local RTC hardware.

ca_opamp_input_t.brief: Defines the signal source for the OPAMP non-inverting input, used during hardware configuration.

members.name: CA_OPAMP_IN_PIN
members.desc: Selects the physical external OPAMPx_VINP pin as the input source.

members.name: CA_OPAMP_IN_DAC
members.desc: Selects the internal DAC channel x output as the input source.

ca_opamp_input_t.notes: This enum is used to configure the internal routing of the STM32 OPAMP peripheral. It does not require allocation or freeing as it is a simple enumeration passed by value to initialization functions.
ca_opamp_input_t.usage: Used in the ca_opamp_init function to specify whether the operational amplifier should sample an external voltage from a pin or an internal voltage generated by the DAC.

ca_p256_pt_t.brief: Represents a point on the P-256 elliptic curve using Jacobian coordinates (x, y, z).

members.name: x
members.desc: The X coordinate of the point, represented as an array of 32-bit limbs.

members.name: y
members.desc: The Y coordinate of the point, represented as an array of 32-bit limbs.

members.name: z
members.desc: The Z coordinate (Jacobian) of the point, represented as an array of 32-bit limbs.

ca_p256_pt_t.notes: This structure is used for internal cryptographic calculations. It is typically allocated on the stack by the caller. The limbs are stored in little-endian format. Ensure the memory is zeroed or initialized before use to avoid processing garbage data.
ca_p256_pt_t.usage: Used as an input or output parameter for low-level ECDSA P-256 operations, such as key generation or point derivation functions within the ca_ecdsa API.

ca_p256_pub_work_t.brief: A workspace structure used to hold intermediate calculation buffers and the resulting public key point during ECDSA P-256 operations.

members.name: d
members.desc: Internal buffer for private key or scalar components. Must be properly initialized before use.

members.name: x
members.desc: Internal buffer for the X-coordinate calculation.

members.name: y
members.desc: Internal buffer for the Y-coordinate calculation.

members.name: Q
members.desc: The resulting public key point structure.

ca_p256_pub_work_t.notes: This structure is intended for stack or heap allocation by the caller. It acts as a scratchpad for the ECDSA P-256 library functions. It does not require specific initialization functions, but ensure the memory is zeroed (e.g., via ca_memzero) before passing it to an API function to avoid using garbage data.
ca_p256_pub_work_t.usage: Used as a mandatory workspace parameter in ECDSA P-256 cryptographic functions such as key generation or public key derivation.

ca_p256_rfc6979_t.brief: Context structure for RFC 6979 deterministic ECDSA signature generation using HMAC-SHA256.

members.name: hmac
members.desc: Internal HMAC-SHA256 context used for the deterministic random bit generator (DRBG) process.

members.name: K
members.desc: Internal HMAC key buffer, 32 bytes.

members.name: V
members.desc: Internal HMAC value buffer, 32 bytes.

members.name: started
members.desc: Flag indicating if the deterministic sequence has been initialized. Must be false before first use.

ca_p256_rfc6979_t.notes: This structure is used internally by the ECDSA signing process to ensure that the nonce 'k' is generated deterministically based on the private key and the message hash. The user is responsible for allocating this struct. It must be zero-initialized or have 'started' set to false before being passed to signing functions.
ca_p256_rfc6979_t.usage: Used as an optional parameter in ECDSA signing functions to provide deterministic nonce generation, preventing security vulnerabilities associated with poor random number sources.

ca_p256_sign_work_t.brief: A workspace structure used to hold intermediate calculations and state during ECDSA P-256 signing operations.

members.name: d, z, k, r, s, km, t, u
members.desc: Internal buffers for big-integer arithmetic limbs. Must not be modified manually.

members.name: hb
members.desc: Buffer for the hashed message (hash bytes).

members.name: st
members.desc: State structure for RFC6979 deterministic nonce generation.

members.name: R
members.desc: Point structure representing the ephemeral public key.

ca_p256_sign_work_t.notes: This structure is large and should be allocated on the stack or in a dedicated memory pool. It is used as a scratchpad by the signing engine; the caller must ensure the memory remains valid for the duration of the ca_ecdsa_p256_sign call. It does not require explicit initialization before passing to the signing function, as the function will initialize the necessary fields.
ca_p256_sign_work_t.usage: Used as an input parameter for the ca_ecdsa_p256_sign function to provide the necessary workspace for the cryptographic computation.

ca_p256_verify_work_t.brief: A workspace structure used to hold intermediate calculation buffers for ECDSA P-256 signature verification.

members.name: r, s, z, w, u1, u2, x, lhs, rhs, t
members.desc: Internal buffers for modular arithmetic operations. Must not be modified manually.

members.name: Q
members.desc: Public key point structure.

members.name: R
members.desc: Resultant point structure used during verification.

ca_p256_verify_work_t.notes: This structure is used as a scratchpad for the ca_ecdsa_p256_verify function. It does not require explicit initialization by the user, but it must be allocated (usually on the stack) before calling the verification function. It does not own any external resources.
ca_p256_verify_work_t.usage: Use this structure when calling ca_ecdsa_p256_verify to provide the necessary memory for the cryptographic math operations. It is typically declared as a local variable in the function performing the signature check.

ca_p256_work_t.brief: A union container used to hold context data for various P-256 ECDSA cryptographic operations.

members.name: hash
members.desc: Context for SHA-256 hashing, used when signing or verifying a message digest.

members.name: sign
members.desc: Workspace structure for ECDSA signing operations.

members.name: verify
members.desc: Workspace structure for ECDSA verification operations.

members.name: pub
members.desc: Workspace structure for public key derivation operations.

ca_p256_work_t.notes: This is a union, meaning only one member can be active at a time. The memory size is determined by the largest member. It is typically allocated on the stack by the caller before invoking an ECDSA function. The caller is responsible for ensuring the correct member is accessed based on the operation being performed.
ca_p256_work_t.usage: Use this type to provide the necessary workspace memory to ca_ecdsa_p256_* functions. It acts as a scratchpad for the cryptographic engine to store intermediate calculations.

ca_pbkdf2_sha256_ctx_t.brief: Context structure for PBKDF2-SHA256 key derivation, used to maintain state during password hashing operations.

members.name: keyed
members.desc: Internal HMAC context initialized with the password; used as the base for subsequent rounds.

members.name: ctx
members.desc: Working HMAC context used to compute the iterative hash rounds.

members.name: u
members.desc: Buffer storing the current block output of the HMAC iteration.

members.name: acc
members.desc: Accumulator buffer storing the XORed result of the hash iterations.

ca_pbkdf2_sha256_ctx_t.notes: This structure is allocated by the caller on the stack or heap. It must be passed to ca_pbkdf2_sha256 to perform the derivation. The structure does not require manual initialization before passing it to the function, as the function will initialize the internal HMAC contexts.
ca_pbkdf2_sha256_ctx_t.usage: Use this structure when you need to derive a cryptographic key from a password using the PBKDF2-SHA256 algorithm. It is passed as an argument to the ca_pbkdf2_sha256 function.

ca_pool_cfg_t.brief: Configuration structure used to define the parameters for creating a thread pool in caOS.

members.name: n_threads
members.desc: The number of worker threads to spawn in the pool. Must be between 1 and 99. Setting this too high may lead to stack overflow or memory exhaustion.

members.name: stack_size
members.desc: The size of the stack allocated for each individual worker thread. Ensure this is large enough for the tasks the threads will perform.

members.name: priority
members.desc: The scheduling priority assigned to the worker threads. Also acts as a fallback configuration for one-shot task execution.

ca_pool_cfg_t.notes: This structure is typically passed by value to pool initialization functions. It does not own any memory itself; it is a template used by the kernel to allocate resources. Ensure the values are within system limits to avoid initialization failure.
ca_pool_cfg_t.usage: Use this structure when you need to initialize a thread pool to manage concurrent tasks. It is passed as an argument to the pool creation API to define the pool's footprint and scheduling behavior.

ca_pwr_info_t.brief: A structure containing the current power and clock configuration status of the STM32 system.

members.name: sysclk_hz
members.desc: Current system clock frequency in Hertz. Used to calculate peripheral timings.

members.name: sysclk_max_hz
members.desc: Maximum rated frequency for the specific board. Used to validate overclocking limits.

members.name: vos
members.desc: Voltage scaling range index. Set to 0xFF if the hardware does not support dynamic voltage scaling (e.g., STM32F1).

members.name: standby_resume
members.desc: Flag indicating if the current execution started after waking up from Standby mode.

members.name: periph_on
members.desc: Bitmask or count of peripherals currently enabled in the RCC (Reset and Clock Control) registers.

members.name: periph_total
members.desc: Total number of peripherals available on the current MCU family.

ca_pwr_info_t.notes: This structure is typically populated by the caOS power driver. It is read-only for the application layer. Do not manually modify these fields as they reflect the hardware state managed by the kernel.
ca_pwr_info_t.usage: Use this structure to perform runtime checks on system performance or to verify if the system is operating within safe power limits before enabling high-consumption peripherals.

ca_pwr_mode_t.brief: An enumeration defining the low-power states available for the STM32 microcontroller in caOS.

members.name: CA_PWR_MODE_SLEEP
members.desc: Executes WFI (Wait For Interrupt) with clocks active. The CPU stops, but peripherals continue running. Wakeup occurs on any interrupt.

members.name: CA_PWR_MODE_STOP
members.desc: Enters deepsleep mode with the low-power regulator. RAM and peripheral states are preserved, but clocks are stopped. Wakeup resumes execution from the point of entry.

members.name: PWR_MODE_STANDBY
members.desc: Enters the lowest power state. RAM content is lost. Wakeup triggers a system reset, effectively restarting the application.

ca_pwr_mode_t.notes: This enum is used to configure the power management unit. Be aware that PWR_MODE_STANDBY causes a full system reset, meaning all volatile data will be lost unless specifically handled in the boot sequence.
ca_pwr_mode_t.usage: Used as an argument in power management API functions to transition the MCU into a specific low-power state to conserve battery life.

ca_pwr_periph_t.brief: Defines the hardware configuration required to enable or disable the clock for a specific STM32 peripheral.

members.name: name
members.desc: Human-readable identifier for the peripheral (e.g., "USART1"). Used primarily for debugging and logging.

members.name: bus
members.desc: The RCC bus name (e.g., "APB1", "APB2", "AHB1"). Used by the driver to identify the clock domain.

members.name: enr
members.desc: Pointer to the specific RCC Enable Register (e.g., &RCC->APB2ENR). Must be a valid volatile memory address.

members.name: mask
members.desc: The specific bit position within the ENR register that controls the peripheral clock. Must be a single bit mask.

ca_pwr_periph_t.notes: This structure is typically defined as a constant global array in the board support package (BSP). It does not require dynamic allocation. The driver treats these as read-only configuration descriptors. Ensure the mask matches the STM32 reference manual for the specific MCU series.
ca_pwr_periph_t.usage: Used by the caOS power management driver to perform low-level clock gating. It is passed to internal driver functions to safely toggle peripheral clocks during initialization or power-saving transitions.

ca_qspi_cfg_t.body:
typedef struct {
u8  clk_div;       /*!< Prescaler: periph_clk / (clk_div + 1)  */
u8  flash_size;    /*!< log2(size_bytes) - 1, e.g. 23 for 16MB */
u8  addr_bytes;    /*!< Address bytes: 3 (24-bit) or 4 (32-bit) */
u8  dummy_cycles;  /*!< Dummy cycles for the read command      */
u8  data_lines;    /*!< Read data lines: 1=single, 2=dual, 4=quad.
Page program uses 4 lines only when this is
4 (0x32), 1 otherwise: there is no dual page
program on W25Q/IS25 parts              */
u8  cmd_read;      /*!< Fast read command, e.g. 0xEB or 0x6B */
u8  cmd_page_prog; /*!< Page program, e.g. 0x32 or 0x02           */
u8  cmd_sector_er; /*!< Sector erase, e.g. 0x20                  */
u8  cmd_wren;      /*!< Write enable, 0x06                       */
u8  cmd_rdsr;      /*!< Read status reg, 0x05                    */
u8  pinmap;        /*!< 0 = Nucleo-144 Zio CN10, 1 = alternate; an
undefined value falls back to 0           */
u8  addr_lines;    /*!< Read address lines: 0/1 = single (0x0B, 0x3B,
0x6B), 2 = dual (0xBB), 4 = quad (0xEB)   */
u8  sample_shift;  /*!< CA_QSPI_SSHIFT_AUTO (0) / _ON / _OFF       */
u8  device;        /*!< CA_QSPI_DEV_NOR (0) / _RAM / _RAW          */
u16 page_size;     /*!< NOR: program page (0 = 256). RAM: largest
transfer under one CS (0 = 256)           */
} ca_qspi_cfg_t;
ca_qspi_cfg_t.brief: Configuration structure used to define the communication parameters and command set for an external QSPI flash memory.

members.name: clk_div
members.desc: Clock prescaler value. The resulting frequency is periph_clk / (clk_div + 1). Ensure this does not exceed the flash chip's maximum rated frequency.

members.name: flash_size
members.desc: Log2 of the total flash size in bytes minus 1. Example: 23 for 16MB (2^24 bytes).

members.name: addr_bytes
members.desc: Number of address bytes used for memory access. Valid values are 3 (24-bit addressing) or 4 (32-bit addressing).

members.name: dummy_cycles
members.desc: Number of dummy cycles required by the flash chip for read operations. Incorrect values will result in corrupted data reads.

members.name: data_lines
members.desc: Number of data lines used for transfer. 1 for Single SPI, 2 for Dual SPI, 4 for Quad SPI.

members.name: cmd_read
members.desc: Opcode for the fast read command (e.g., 0xEB for Quad I/O Read).

members.name: cmd_page_prog
members.desc: Opcode for the page program command (e.g., 0x32 for Quad Page Program).

members.name: cmd_sector_er
members.desc: Opcode for the sector erase command (e.g., 0x20 for 4KB sector erase).

members.name: cmd_wren
members.desc: Opcode for the Write Enable command, typically 0x06.

members.name: cmd_rdsr
members.desc: Opcode for reading the flash status register, typically 0x05.

ca_qspi_cfg_t.notes: This struct is passed by value or pointer to the QSPI driver initialization function. It must be populated based on the specific datasheet of the external flash chip connected to the STM32. The user is responsible for ensuring the values match the hardware capabilities.
ca_qspi_cfg_t.usage: Used during the initialization phase of the QSPI peripheral to configure the communication protocol and command set required to interface with external flash memory.

ca_qspi_pin_t.brief: An enumeration representing the specific physical pins used by the QSPI peripheral interface.

members.name: CA_QSPI_PIN_CLK
members.desc: The Serial Clock pin.

members.name: CA_QSPI_PIN_NCS
members.desc: The Chip Select (active low) pin.

members.name: CA_QSPI_PIN_IO0
members.desc: Data line 0 (often MOSI in single-line mode).

members.name: CA_QSPI_PIN_IO1
members.desc: Data line 1 (often MISO in single-line mode).

members.name: CA_QSPI_PIN_IO2
members.desc: Data line 2.

members.name: CA_QSPI_PIN_IO3
members.desc: Data line 3.

members.name: CA_QSPI_PIN_COUNT
members.desc: Helper value representing the total number of pins; do not use as a valid pin index.

ca_qspi_pin_t.notes: This enum is used to index into configuration arrays or pin mapping tables. CA_QSPI_PIN_COUNT is provided to allow for easy array sizing and bounds checking. Ensure that the hardware design matches the pin mapping expected by the driver.
ca_qspi_pin_t.usage: Used primarily in driver configuration structures or initialization functions where specific GPIO pins must be assigned to the QSPI peripheral functionality.
ca_qspi_pin_t.example: ca_qspi_pin_t pin = CA_QSPI_PIN_CLK; if (pin < CA_QSPI_PIN_COUNT) { /* Proceed with pin configuration */ }

ca_qspi_xfer_t.brief: A structure defining the parameters for a single QSPI bus transaction, used to configure command, address, and data phases.

members.name: cmd
members.desc: The 8-bit instruction code to send to the QSPI device.

members.name: cmd_lines
members.desc: Number of data lines used for the command phase. Valid: 0 or 1 (Single), 2, or 4 (QPI).

members.name: addr_bytes
members.desc: Number of address bytes to transmit. Set to 0 to use the default configured value.

members.name: addr_lines
members.desc: Number of data lines used for the address phase.

members.name: addr
members.desc: The memory address on the external device to access.

members.name: dummy
members.desc: Number of dummy cycles required by the device before data transfer.

members.name: data_lines
members.desc: Number of data lines used for the data phase. Set to 0 if no data phase is required.

members.name: read
members.desc: Direction of the data phase. True for read (device to MCU), false for write (MCU to device).

members.name: rx
members.desc: Pointer to the buffer where received data will be stored. Only used if read is true.

members.name: tx
members.desc: Pointer to the buffer containing data to be sent. Only used if read is false.

members.name: len
members.desc: Number of bytes to transfer during the data phase.

ca_qspi_xfer_t.notes: The structure must be fully initialized before passing it to the driver. Ensure that the buffers pointed to by rx or tx remain valid for the duration of the transfer. This struct is typically allocated on the stack by the caller.
ca_qspi_xfer_t.usage: Used as an argument for QSPI transfer functions to perform read/write operations on external flash or memory-mapped devices.

ca_queue_static_t.body:
typedef struct {
u32 item_size;               // Single item size (bytes)
u32 max_items;               // Maximum capacity
volatile u32 count;          // Number of items present
volatile u32 head;           // Read index (consumer)
volatile u32 tail;           // Write index (producer)
ca_wait_queue_t wait_send;       // Task waiting for send (queue full)
ca_wait_queue_t wait_recv;       // Task waiting for receive (queue empty)
ca_spinlock_irq_t lock;          // Concurrent access protection
u8 buffer[];                 // Flexible array member (inline buffer)
} ca_queue_static_t;
ca_queue_static_t.brief: A statically allocated FIFO queue structure used for thread-safe data exchange between tasks.

members.name: item_size
members.desc: Size of a single element in the queue in bytes.

members.name: max_items
members.desc: Maximum number of items the queue can hold.

members.name: count
members.desc: Current number of items stored in the queue.

members.name: head
members.desc: Index for the next read operation.

members.name: tail
members.desc: Index for the next write operation.

members.name: wait_send
members.desc: Internal wait queue for tasks blocked while trying to send to a full queue.

members.name: wait_recv
members.desc: Internal wait queue for tasks blocked while trying to receive from an empty queue.

members.name: lock
members.desc: Spinlock used to ensure atomic access to the queue structure.

members.name: buffer
members.desc: Flexible array member acting as the storage area for queue items.

ca_queue_static_t.notes: The structure must be declared with enough space for the buffer. Since it uses a flexible array member, you typically define a wrapper struct containing the queue and a static array. It is initialized via ca_queue_static_init. Ownership is usually shared between producer and consumer tasks.
ca_queue_static_t.usage: Use this when you need a fixed-size, thread-safe FIFO buffer. It is ideal for passing data between ISRs and tasks or between two tasks without dynamic memory allocation.

ca_queue_t.body:
typedef struct {
u8 *buffer;                  // Buffer items (allocated on heap)
u32 item_size;               // Single item size (bytes)
u32 max_items;               // Maximum capacity
volatile u32 count;          // Number of items present
volatile u32 head;           // Read index (consumer)
volatile u32 tail;           // Write index (producer)
ca_wait_queue_t wait_send;       // Task waiting for send (queue full)
ca_wait_queue_t wait_recv;       // Task waiting for receive (queue empty)
ca_spinlock_irq_t lock;          // Concurrent access protection
} ca_queue_t;
ca_queue_t.brief: A thread-safe FIFO queue structure used for inter-task communication and data buffering.

members.name: buffer
members.desc: Pointer to the memory area storing the queue items. Must be allocated before initialization.

members.name: item_size
members.desc: Size of a single element in bytes.

members.name: max_items
members.desc: Maximum number of items the queue can hold.

members.name: count
members.desc: Current number of items in the queue.

members.name: head
members.desc: Index for the next read operation.

members.name: tail
members.desc: Index for the next write operation.

members.name: wait_send
members.desc: Internal wait queue for tasks blocked on a full queue.

members.name: wait_recv
members.desc: Internal wait queue for tasks blocked on an empty queue.

members.name: lock
members.desc: Spinlock used to ensure atomic access to the queue structure.

ca_queue_t.notes: The structure is typically initialized via ca_queue_heap_init or ca_queue_static_init. The user is responsible for providing the memory buffer if using static initialization. The internal spinlock handles concurrency, making it safe to use between tasks and ISRs.
ca_queue_t.usage: Use this type to pass data between producer and consumer tasks. It is the core structure for the ca_queue_* API family, which provides thread-safe push and pop operations.

ca_recursive_mutex_t.brief: A synchronization primitive that allows the same task to acquire the lock multiple times without deadlocking itself.

members.name: owner
members.desc: Stores the handle of the task currently holding the mutex. Only valid if lock_count > 0.

members.name: lock_count
members.desc: Tracks the nesting level of the lock. Incremented on lock, decremented on unlock. 0 means the mutex is available.

members.name: wait_queue
members.desc: Internal list of tasks blocked waiting for this mutex.

members.name: internal_lock
members.desc: Low-level spinlock used to ensure atomic access to the structure members during state changes.

ca_recursive_mutex_t.notes: The recursive mutex must be initialized using ca_rmutex_init before use. It is typically allocated in the global data segment or as part of a larger control structure. The owner must be the same task that performs the unlock; attempting to unlock a mutex held by another task is undefined behavior.
ca_recursive_mutex_t.usage: Use this when a task needs to call multiple functions that all require the same resource, and each function independently attempts to lock the resource. It prevents the task from blocking on its own held lock.

ca_route_entry_t.brief: Represents a single entry in the system routing table used to determine the next hop for outgoing network packets.

members.name: dst
members.desc: The destination IPv4 address or network prefix. Must be a valid IPv4 structure.

members.name: mask
members.desc: The subnet mask associated with the destination. Defines the range of the network.

members.name: gw
members.desc: The gateway (next hop) IP address. If the destination is local, this may be set to 0.0.0.0.

members.name: active
members.desc: Status flag. Set to true to enable the route, false to ignore it during lookup.

ca_route_entry_t.notes: The routing table is typically managed by the network stack. Ensure that the mask is correctly aligned with the destination address to avoid routing loops or unreachable destinations. This struct is usually allocated in static memory or as part of a configuration array.
ca_route_entry_t.usage: Used when configuring static routes in the network stack or when querying the routing table to determine how to forward packets to specific subnets.

ca_rtc_alarm_cb_t.brief: A function pointer type used to define a callback function that executes when a specific RTC alarm triggers.

members.name: alarm_id
members.desc: The identifier of the alarm that triggered the event. Valid values are typically 0 or 1 depending on the hardware configuration. Providing an invalid ID may lead to logic errors in the handler.

ca_rtc_alarm_cb_t.notes: This callback is executed within the context of the RTC interrupt service routine (ISR). Therefore, the function must be kept extremely short, must not perform blocking operations (like waiting for semaphores or mutexes), and should avoid heavy processing. The user is responsible for defining the function and passing its address to the RTC driver configuration.
ca_rtc_alarm_cb_t.usage: Use this type when you need to perform an action (e.g., setting a flag, waking a task) immediately upon an RTC alarm event. It is typically passed as an argument during the RTC initialization or alarm configuration phase.

ca_rtc_alarm_t.brief: A configuration structure used to define the trigger conditions for a Real-Time Clock (RTC) alarm event.

members.name: sec
members.desc: Seconds value for the alarm. Valid range: 0-59. Ignored if match_sec is false.

members.name: min
members.desc: Minutes value for the alarm. Valid range: 0-59. Ignored if match_min is false.

members.name: hour
members.desc: Hours value for the alarm (24h format). Valid range: 0-23. Ignored if match_hour is false.

members.name: day
members.desc: Day of the month for the alarm. Valid range: 1-31. Ignored if match_day is false.

members.name: match_sec
members.desc: If true, the RTC will trigger the alarm when the current seconds match the 'sec' field.

members.name: match_min
members.desc: If true, the RTC will trigger the alarm when the current minutes match the 'min' field.

members.name: match_hour
members.desc: If true, the RTC will trigger the alarm when the current hours match the 'hour' field.

members.name: match_day
members.desc: If true, the RTC will trigger the alarm when the current day matches the 'day' field.

ca_rtc_alarm_t.notes: The structure is typically allocated on the stack by the user. The RTC hardware only checks fields where the corresponding match flag is set to true. If all match flags are false, the alarm behavior is undefined or may never trigger.
ca_rtc_alarm_t.usage: Use this structure to configure an RTC alarm via the caOS driver API. Populate the fields, set the desired match flags, and pass the structure pointer to the RTC alarm configuration function.
ca_rtc_alarm_t.example: ca_rtc_alarm_t my_alarm = { .sec = 30, .match_sec = true, .match_min = false, .match_hour = false, .match_day = false }; ca_rtc_set_alarm(&my_alarm);

ca_rtc_clk_src_t.brief: Defines the clock source selection for the Real-Time Clock (RTC) peripheral.

members.name: CA_RTC_CLK_LSE
members.desc: External 32.768 kHz crystal. Provides the highest accuracy for timekeeping.

members.name: CA_RTC_CLK_LSI
members.desc: Internal Low-Speed RC oscillator. Does not require external components but is less accurate and temperature-dependent.

members.name: CA_RTC_CLK_HSE
members.desc: High-Speed External clock divided by 32. Used when an external crystal is available but LSE is not populated.

ca_rtc_clk_src_t.notes: The clock source must be configured before initializing the RTC peripheral. Changing the clock source while the RTC is running may cause unpredictable behavior or time drift. Ensure the hardware board actually supports the selected source (e.g., verify the presence of an LSE crystal).
ca_rtc_clk_src_t.usage: Used during the RTC initialization phase to tell the driver which hardware oscillator to use as the timebase for the RTC counter.

ca_rtc_dt_t.brief: A structure representing a calendar date and time for the RTC peripheral.

members.name: sec
members.desc: Seconds, range 0-59. Values outside this range may cause hardware errors.

members.name: min
members.desc: Minutes, range 0-59.

members.name: hour
members.desc: Hours in 24-hour format, range 0-23.

members.name: wday
members.desc: Day of the week, range 1-7 where 1 is Monday.

members.name: day
members.desc: Day of the month, range 1-31.

members.name: month
members.desc: Month of the year, range 1-12.

members.name: year
members.desc: Year offset from 2000, range 0-99 (e.g., 24 represents 2024).

ca_rtc_dt_t.notes: This struct is used to interface with the RTC hardware. It does not perform validation; ensure values are within the specified ranges before passing to driver functions to avoid undefined behavior in the RTC peripheral.
ca_rtc_dt_t.usage: Used as a parameter for RTC driver functions to set or retrieve the current system time and date.

ca_rwlock_t.brief: A synchronization primitive that allows multiple concurrent readers or a single exclusive writer to access a shared resource.

members.name: readers
members.desc: Counter of currently active readers. Incremented when a reader acquires the lock, decremented when released.

members.name: writer_active
members.desc: Flag indicating if a writer currently holds the lock. 1 if active, 0 otherwise.

members.name: read_queue
members.desc: Queue of tasks blocked waiting to acquire the lock for reading.

members.name: write_queue
members.desc: Queue of tasks blocked waiting to acquire the lock for writing.

members.name: internal_lock
members.desc: Internal spinlock used to ensure atomic access to the rwlock structure members during state changes.

ca_rwlock_t.notes: The structure must be initialized before use. It is typically allocated in static memory or as part of a larger control block. Ownership is shared among tasks accessing the resource. Do not modify members directly; use the provided ca_rwlock API functions to ensure thread safety.
ca_rwlock_t.usage: Use this when you have a data structure that is read frequently but updated rarely. It improves performance over a standard mutex by allowing multiple readers to access the data simultaneously while ensuring exclusive access for writers.

ca_sai_config_t.brief: Configuration structure for the Serial Audio Interface (SAI) peripheral, defining sample rate, bit depth, and protocol.

members.name: fs_hz
members.desc: The desired audio sample rate in Hertz (e.g., 44100, 48000). Must be supported by the hardware clock configuration.

members.name: bits
members.desc: Data word length in bits. Valid values are 16, 24, or 32.

members.name: proto
members.desc: The audio protocol mode (e.g., I2S, Left-Justified, Right-Justified). Must be a valid enum value from ca_sai_proto_t.

ca_sai_config_t.notes: This struct is passed by value to the initialization function. It does not require dynamic allocation; it is typically declared on the stack before calling the initialization routine. Ensure the hardware clock is configured to support the requested fs_hz before calling ca_sai_init.
ca_sai_config_t.usage: Used as an input parameter for the ca_sai_init function to configure the SAI peripheral hardware registers before starting audio streaming.

ca_sai_proto_t.brief: Defines the digital audio protocol format (I2S or MSB-justified) used for SAI peripheral communication.

members.name: CA_SAI_I2S
members.desc: Standard Philips I2S format. Frame Sync (FS) is low for the left channel; data is delayed by one bit clock cycle relative to FS.

members.name: CA_SAI_MSB
members.desc: MSB-justified format. Frame Sync (FS) is high for the left channel; data is aligned exactly with the FS edge.

ca_sai_proto_t.notes: This enum is used to configure the hardware interface behavior. Ensure the selected protocol matches the requirements of your external audio codec or DAC/ADC chip. Incorrect selection will result in bit-shifted or garbled audio data.
ca_sai_proto_t.usage: Used during the initialization of the SAI peripheral to specify the data alignment and framing protocol.

ca_scheduler_tasks_info_mode.brief: An enumeration used to specify the level of detail or the specific category of information to retrieve when querying task statistics.

members.name: CA_TH_INFO_DEFAULT
members.desc: Retrieves standard task information. Use this for general monitoring.

members.name: CA_TH_INFO_FLAG
members.desc: Retrieves task flag status. Useful for debugging task state transitions.

members.name: TH_INFO_RUNTIME
members.desc: Retrieves execution time statistics. Essential for profiling and identifying bottlenecks.

members.name: CA_TH_INFO_MEM
members.desc: Retrieves stack usage and memory allocation data. Critical for preventing stack overflows.

members.name: TH_INFO_ASSERT
members.desc: Retrieves assertion-related diagnostic data. Used primarily for error tracking.

ca_scheduler_tasks_info_mode.notes: This enum is passed as an argument to scheduler diagnostic functions. It does not require manual allocation as it is a simple integer-based enumeration. Ensure the mode passed is supported by the specific diagnostic function being called to avoid undefined behavior.
ca_scheduler_tasks_info_mode.usage: Use this type when calling scheduler diagnostic APIs to filter the output data. It allows you to request only the specific metrics needed, reducing overhead and keeping logs clean.

ca_secure_key_entry_t.brief: Represents a metadata entry for a cryptographic key stored in the secure common area.

members.name: base_address
members.desc: The starting memory address of the key in the secure storage area. Must be aligned according to hardware requirements.

members.name: size
members.desc: The size of the key in bytes. Must match the actual key data length to prevent buffer overflows.

members.name: validity_start
members.desc: Packed date format representing when the key becomes active. Set to 0 to disable this check.

members.name: validity_stop
members.desc: Packed date format representing when the key expires. Set to 0 to disable this check.

members.name: is_allocated
members.desc: Boolean flag indicating if the entry is currently in use. 1 for allocated, 0 for free.

members.name: access_mode
members.desc: Bitmask defining read/write/execute permissions for the key. Incorrect values may cause hardware access faults.

members.name: key_id
members.desc: A unique identifier used to reference the key during cryptographic operations.

ca_secure_key_entry_t.notes: This structure is typically managed by the caOS key store manager. The application should treat this as read-only unless using specific management APIs. Ensure the memory region pointed to by base_address is initialized before setting is_allocated to 1.
ca_secure_key_entry_t.usage: Used when querying the key store for metadata or when registering a new key into the secure storage system via the caOS crypto subsystem.

ca_secure_pipe_end_t.brief: Identifies the specific endpoint (A or B) of a secure communication pipe.

members.name: CA_SECURE_PIPE_A
members.desc: Represents the first endpoint of the secure pipe. Must be used consistently with the peer configuration.

members.name: CA_SECURE_PIPE_B
members.desc: Represents the second endpoint of the secure pipe. Must be used consistently with the peer configuration.

ca_secure_pipe_end_t.notes: This enum is used to distinguish between the two sides of a secure pipe connection. It is typically passed to initialization or communication functions to ensure data is routed to the correct logical channel. Ensure that the local and remote ends are configured to use opposite identifiers if required by the protocol.
ca_secure_pipe_end_t.usage: Used as a parameter in ca_secure_pipe_init, ca_secure_pipe_send, and ca_secure_pipe_recv to specify which pipe end is being accessed.

ca_secure_pipe_t.brief: Represents a secure, encrypted communication channel between two endpoints using AES encryption.

members.name: ch
members.desc: The underlying AES cryptographic channel used for encrypting and decrypting data.

members.name: q
members.desc: Two internal queues: q[0] holds ciphertext for endpoint 0, q[1] for endpoint 1. Do not manipulate these directly.

members.name: ready
members.desc: Flag indicating if the pipe is fully initialized and ready for secure data transmission.

ca_secure_pipe_t.notes: The structure must be initialized via ca_secure_pipe_init. The user is responsible for allocating the memory for the struct, but the internal queues and AES channel are managed by the ca_secure_pipe service. Ensure the pipe is deinitialized with ca_secure_pipe_deinit before freeing the memory to prevent resource leaks.
ca_secure_pipe_t.usage: Used to establish a secure, encrypted data stream between two tasks or system components. Use ca_secure_pipe_send to push data into the pipe and ca_secure_pipe_recv to retrieve decrypted data from the other end.

ca_sem_name_t.brief: A union used to provide a unique identifier for a semaphore, allowing it to be represented as either an 8-character string or a 64-bit integer.

members.name: name_c
members.desc: An array of 8 characters. Used for human-readable names. If the string is shorter than 8 bytes, ensure the remaining bytes are null-terminated.

members.name: name_l
members.desc: A 64-bit integer representation of the name. Useful for faster comparisons or when a numeric ID is preferred over a string.

ca_sem_name_t.notes: This is a union, meaning both members share the same memory location. Writing to name_c will overwrite name_l and vice versa. It is typically passed by value to semaphore creation functions. No dynamic allocation is required as it is usually declared on the stack or as a static member.
ca_sem_name_t.usage: Used when initializing a semaphore to give it a unique name for debugging or tracking purposes within the RTOS kernel. It is passed as an argument to semaphore initialization functions to identify the resource.
ca_sem_name_t.example: ca_sem_name_t my_sem_name; my_sem_name.name_c[0] = 'U'; my_sem_name.name_c[1] = 'A'; my_sem_name.name_c[2] = 'R'; my_sem_name.name_c[3] = 'T'; my_sem_name.name_c[4] = '\0'; // Initialize semaphore with this name

ca_semaphore_t.brief: A counting semaphore used to manage access to a limited number of shared resources or to synchronize tasks.

members.name: count
members.desc: Current number of available resources. Decremented by wait, incremented by post.

members.name: max_count
members.desc: The upper limit for the semaphore count. Prevents overflow if set correctly.

members.name: wait_queue
members.desc: Internal list of tasks currently blocked waiting for this semaphore.

members.name: internal_lock
members.desc: Spinlock used to ensure atomic access to the semaphore structure members.

members.name: name
members.desc: Optional string identifier for debugging purposes.

ca_semaphore_t.notes: The semaphore must be initialized using ca_sem_init before use. It is typically allocated in the global data segment or as part of a larger control structure. Ownership is usually shared among tasks that need to synchronize. Do not modify members directly; always use the ca_sem_* API functions.
ca_semaphore_t.usage: Use this type when you need to limit the number of tasks accessing a resource (e.g., a pool of buffers) or to signal between tasks. Use ca_sem_init to set the initial and maximum count, ca_sem_wait to acquire a resource, and ca_sem_post to release it.

ca_sha256_ctx_t.brief: A structure holding the internal state and working memory for the SHA-256 hashing algorithm.

members.name: state
members.desc: The internal hash state (H0-H7). Initialized by ca_sha256_init and updated during processing.

members.name: bitlen
members.desc: Total length of the message processed so far in bits. Must be updated correctly to ensure final hash integrity.

members.name: buffer
members.desc: Temporary storage for incoming data chunks that are not yet a full 64-byte block.

members.name: buflen
members.desc: Number of valid bytes currently stored in the buffer. Must be less than 64.

members.name: W
members.desc: Message schedule array. Stored in the context to prevent stack overflow on memory-constrained targets like STM32F407.

ca_sha256_ctx_t.notes: The context must be initialized using ca_sha256_init before any update or finalization. It is typically allocated by the caller (on the stack or as a static/global variable). The user is responsible for the memory lifecycle of this struct. Do not manually modify these fields; use the provided API functions.
ca_sha256_ctx_t.usage: Use this type to maintain the state of a SHA-256 calculation across multiple data chunks. It is passed as a pointer to ca_sha256_init, ca_sha256_update, and ca_sha256_final.
ca_sha256_ctx_t.example: ca_sha256_ctx_t ctx; uint8_t hash[32]; ca_sha256_init(&ctx); ca_sha256_update(&ctx, (uint8_t*)"hello", 5); ca_sha256_final(&ctx, hash);

ca_sha512_ctx_t.brief: A context structure used to maintain the internal state of a SHA-512 hashing operation across multiple data chunks.

members.name: state
members.desc: The internal hash state (H0-H7). Initialized by the hash start function.

members.name: bitlen_lo
members.desc: Lower 64 bits of the total message length in bits. Used for final padding.

members.name: bitlen_hi
members.desc: Upper 64 bits of the total message length in bits.

members.name: buffer
members.desc: Temporary storage for incoming data that does not yet fill a full 128-byte block.

members.name: buflen
members.desc: Number of valid bytes currently stored in the buffer. Must be less than 128.

members.name: W
members.desc: Message schedule array. Stored here to prevent stack overflow in deep call stacks.

ca_sha512_ctx_t.notes: The structure must be initialized before use. It is typically allocated by the caller on the stack or as a static variable. It does not require dynamic memory allocation (malloc). Do not manually modify the fields after initialization.
ca_sha512_ctx_t.usage: Use this structure when you need to hash data that arrives in fragments or is too large to fit in memory at once. Pass a pointer to this struct to the initialization, update, and finalization functions of the SHA-512 API.

ca_sp_link_stats_t.brief: A structure containing diagnostic counters for a secure pipe link, used to monitor connection health and security events.

members.name: hello_ok
members.desc: Number of successful handshake attempts.

members.name: hello_bad
members.desc: Number of failed handshake attempts.

members.name: sessions
members.desc: Total number of session keys successfully derived.

members.name: sealed
members.desc: Number of packets successfully encrypted/sealed.

members.name: opened
members.desc: Number of packets successfully decrypted/opened.

members.name: tag_fail
members.desc: Count of authentication failures (forged or tampered data).

members.name: replay
members.desc: Count of packets rejected due to replay protection (duplicate or out-of-window).

members.name: bad_format
members.desc: Count of packets rejected due to malformed headers or invalid lengths.

ca_sp_link_stats_t.notes: This structure is typically populated by the secure pipe service. It is a read-only snapshot for the user. The application does not need to allocate memory for it; it is usually passed as a pointer to be filled by the underlying secure pipe driver.
ca_sp_link_stats_t.usage: Use this to monitor the security integrity of a communication channel. If 'tag_fail' or 'replay' counters increase rapidly, it may indicate an active attack or severe synchronization issues between peers.

ca_sp_link_t.brief: Represents the state and cryptographic context of a secure communication pipe between two nodes.

members.name: role
members.desc: Defines the node role (1 or 2). Used to determine key derivation order.

members.name: ready
members.desc: Indicates if the structure has been successfully initialized.

members.name: up
members.desc: Indicates if session keys are derived and the pipe is ready for encrypted traffic.

members.name: my_fresh
members.desc: Flag indicating if the local nonce has been sent but pairing is incomplete.

members.name: peer_pending
members.desc: Flag indicating a peer nonce is waiting for a local hello response.

members.name: my_nonce
members.desc: Local random nonce used for session key derivation.

members.name: peer_nonce
members.desc: Remote peer nonce used for session key derivation.

members.name: k_tx, k_rx
members.desc: Pointers to static direction keys stored in the keys_store.

members.name: s_tx, s_rx
members.desc: Pointers to session AES contexts; initialized once per session.

members.name: ctx
members.desc: Pointer to heap-allocated AES context, re-initialized per message.

members.name: mutex
members.desc: Mutex to ensure thread-safe access to the pipe state.

members.name: tx_ctr
members.desc: Monotonic counter for outgoing messages to prevent replay attacks.

members.name: rx_top
members.desc: Highest sequence number accepted from the peer.

members.name: rx_win
members.desc: Sliding window bitmask for tracking accepted incoming sequence numbers.

members.name: session_ms
members.desc: Timestamp (ca_os_tick_ms) when the session was established.

members.name: st
members.desc: Statistics structure for tracking pipe performance and errors.

ca_sp_link_t.notes: The structure must be initialized via ca_sp_link_init. The 'ctx' member is heap-allocated and must be managed carefully to avoid leaks. The mutex must be locked before accessing any fields during transmission or reception. Ownership of the link structure is typically held by the task managing the secure connection.
ca_sp_link_t.usage: Used by the secure pipe service to maintain session state. It is passed as a handle to functions like ca_sp_link_hello, ca_sp_link_accept, and ca_sp_link_seal to perform cryptographic operations and manage the secure channel lifecycle.

ca_spi_br_t.brief: Defines the baud rate prescaler for the SPI peripheral, determining the communication speed relative to the peripheral clock.

members.name: CA_SPI_BR_DIV2 to CA_SPI_BR_DIV256
members.desc: Sets the divisor for the SPI peripheral clock (FPCLK). Higher divisors result in slower communication speeds. Ensure the resulting frequency does not exceed the maximum rating of the connected slave device.

ca_spi_br_t.notes: This enum is used to configure the hardware clock divider. The actual SPI frequency is calculated as FPCLK / (2^n), where n is the value of the enum. It must be set during the SPI initialization phase before the peripheral is enabled.
ca_spi_br_t.usage: Used within the SPI configuration structure passed to the initialization function to set the desired bit rate for synchronous serial communication.

ca_spi_config_t.body:
typedef struct {
u8                spi_num;     /* 1=SPI1, 2=SPI2, 3=SPI3          */
ca_spi_br_t       br;          /* clock prescaler (master only)    */
u8                cpol;        /* 0=idle low,  1=idle high         */
u8                cpha;        /* 0=1st edge,  1=2nd edge          */
bool              master;      /* true=master, false=slave         */
u16               frame_size;  /* bytes per frame (slave IRQ mode)  */
ca_spi_slave_cb_t on_rx;       /* NULL=polling, non-NULL=IRQ slave */
bool              alternate_gpio; /* true=alternative pin mapping   */
bool              manage_cs;   /* true=driver manages CS via GPIO */
u8                slave_tx_fill; /* slave IRQ: byte answered on MISO for each byte in, 0=none */
ca_gpio_port_t       cs_port;     /* CS GPIO port                */
ca_gpio_pin_t        cs_pin;      /* CS GPIO pin                  */
} ca_spi_config_t;
ca_spi_config_t.brief: Configuration structure used to define the hardware parameters and operating mode of an SPI peripheral.

members.name: spi_num
members.desc: The hardware SPI instance index. Valid values are 1, 2, or 3. Incorrect values will cause driver initialization to fail.

members.name: br
members.desc: Baud rate prescaler for master mode. Determines the SPI clock speed. Must be set according to the peripheral's maximum clock frequency.

members.name: cpol
members.desc: Clock polarity: 0 for idle low, 1 for idle high. Must match the slave device's requirements.

members.name: cpha
members.desc: Clock phase: 0 for first edge capture, 1 for second edge capture. Must match the slave device's requirements.

members.name: master
members.desc: Sets the SPI role. True for master (generates clock), false for slave (receives clock).

members.name: frame_size
members.desc: Expected number of bytes per frame when operating in slave IRQ mode.

members.name: on_rx
members.desc: Callback function pointer for slave IRQ mode. If set to NULL, the driver operates in polling mode.

members.name: alternate_gpio
members.desc: If true, uses the alternate pin mapping for the SPI peripheral pins.

members.name: manage_cs
members.desc: If true, the driver automatically toggles the Chip Select pin defined by cs_port and cs_pin.

members.name: cs_port
members.desc: GPIO port identifier for the Chip Select signal.

members.name: cs_pin
members.desc: GPIO pin number for the Chip Select signal.

ca_spi_config_t.notes: This structure is typically allocated on the stack before calling the SPI initialization function. Ensure all fields are initialized to avoid undefined behavior. If manage_cs is true, ensure the GPIO port and pin are correctly configured as outputs before SPI initialization.
ca_spi_config_t.usage: Used as an input parameter for the SPI driver initialization function to configure the peripheral hardware settings before any data transfer occurs.
ca_spi_config_t.example: ca_spi_config_t spi_cfg = { .spi_num = 1, .br = CA_SPI_BR_DIV8, .cpol = 0, .cpha = 0, .master = true, .manage_cs = true, .cs_port = GPIOA, .cs_pin = GPIO_PIN_4 }; ca_spi_init(&spi_cfg);

ca_spi_slave_cb_t.body: typedef void (*ca_spi_slave_cb_t)(u8 spi_num, const u8 *data, u16 len)
ca_spi_slave_cb_t.brief: A function pointer type used as a callback to handle incoming data when the STM32 is configured as an SPI slave.

members.name: spi_num
members.desc: The index of the SPI peripheral that received the data (e.g., 1 for SPI1). Must match the hardware peripheral ID.

members.name: data
members.desc: Pointer to the buffer containing the received bytes. This memory is managed by the driver and should be treated as read-only.

members.name: len
members.desc: The number of bytes received in the current transaction. Must be used to avoid buffer overflows when processing data.

ca_spi_slave_cb_t.notes: This callback is executed in the context of the SPI interrupt service routine. Keep the logic inside this function extremely brief to avoid blocking other system tasks. Do not perform blocking operations or complex calculations here. The pointer 'data' is only valid for the duration of the callback execution.
ca_spi_slave_cb_t.usage: Used when initializing an SPI slave interface via the caOS driver. You assign a function matching this signature to the driver configuration structure so the system knows where to route incoming SPI data.

ca_spinlock_irq_t.brief: A spinlock structure that automatically disables interrupts to ensure thread safety in both task and ISR contexts.

members.name: key
members.desc: Internal flag used to track the lock state. Must be initialized to 0.

members.name: irq_state
members.desc: Storage for the CPU interrupt mask state saved during lock acquisition to restore it correctly upon release.

ca_spinlock_irq_t.notes: This structure must be initialized using ca_spinlock_irq_init before use. It is typically allocated as a static variable or within a global control block. It is designed to prevent deadlocks when a resource is shared between tasks and interrupt service routines (ISRs).
ca_spinlock_irq_t.usage: Use this type when you need to protect a shared resource (like a global variable or hardware peripheral) that is accessed by both normal tasks and ISRs. Use ca_spinlock_lock_irq to acquire and ca_spinlock_unlock_irq to release.

ca_spinlock_t.brief: A lightweight synchronization primitive used to protect shared resources by busy-waiting.

members.name: key
members.desc: Internal state of the spinlock. Must be treated as opaque; do not modify directly.

ca_spinlock_t.notes: Spinlocks are intended for very short critical sections. They do not put the task to sleep, meaning the CPU will spin in a loop until the lock is acquired. Using them for long operations will starve other tasks and degrade system performance. Always initialize before use.
ca_spinlock_t.usage: Use when you need to protect data accessed by both ISRs and tasks, or between tasks where the critical section is extremely short. Use ca_spinlock_lock_irq and ca_spinlock_unlock_irq for ISR-safe protection.

ca_stream_buffer_t.brief: A thread-safe, circular FIFO buffer used for streaming byte-oriented data between tasks or ISRs.

members.name: buffer
members.desc: Pointer to the allocated memory block used for storage.

members.name: size
members.desc: Total capacity of the buffer in bytes.

members.name: head
members.desc: Index where the next byte will be written.

members.name: tail
members.desc: Index where the next byte will be read.

members.name: count
members.desc: Current number of bytes stored in the buffer.

members.name: lock
members.desc: Internal spinlock to ensure atomic access during concurrent operations.

members.name: waiting_task
members.desc: Handle of the task waiting for data; set to CA_TASK_HANDLE_NONE if no task is waiting.

members.name: trigger_level
members.desc: Threshold of bytes required to trigger a task wake-up event.

ca_stream_buffer_t.notes: The structure must be initialized via ca_stream_init before use. The memory for the buffer must be allocated by the user (e.g., via ca_memory_allocate) and must persist for the lifetime of the stream. The 'volatile' fields ensure that the compiler does not optimize away memory accesses, which is critical for ISR-to-task communication.
ca_stream_buffer_t.usage: Used for buffering data streams (e.g., UART RX/TX, network data). Use ca_stream_send/ca_stream_receive for data transfer, and ca_stream_set_trigger to define when a blocked task should be unblocked.

ca_sw_timer_handle_t.brief: A unique identifier (handle) used to reference and manage a software timer within the caOS RTOS.

members.name: ca_sw_timer_handle_t
members.desc: An 8-bit unsigned integer acting as an index or ID for a specific software timer. Valid values range from 0 to the maximum number of timers configured in the system.

ca_sw_timer_handle_t.notes: This type is a simple alias for an unsigned 8-bit integer. It does not represent the timer object itself, but rather a reference to it. The handle is typically returned by the timer creation function and must be stored by the user to perform subsequent operations like starting, stopping, or deleting the timer. It is not dynamically allocated; it is a stack or global variable.
ca_sw_timer_handle_t.usage: Use this type whenever you need to interact with a software timer after it has been created. It is passed as the first argument to functions such as ca_sw_timer_start, ca_sw_timer_stop, and ca_sw_timer_delete to specify which timer instance to target.

ca_sw_timer_mode_t.brief: An enumeration defining the execution behavior of a software timer in caOS.

members.name: CA_TIMER_ONE_SHOT
members.desc: The timer callback will execute exactly once after the timeout period expires. The timer stops automatically after the first trigger.

members.name: CA_TIMER_PERIODIC
members.desc: The timer callback will execute repeatedly at the specified interval until explicitly stopped by the user.
